## 1. Welcome and Our Values

Welcome to Harbourlight Analytics. You are joining a team of thirty data consultants who are passionate about helping clients see their data more clearly. We have grown from eight people to thirty in eighteen months, and while we have more faces around the office (and on video calls) than we did at the start, our culture hasn’t changed. We are a group of professionals who support each other, respect each other’s time, and take pride in doing good work.

We don’t have a rulebook for every human interaction, but we do have four values that guide how we treat each other and our clients. These aren’t just posters on a wall; they are the tools we use to make decisions when there isn’t a clear right answer. Here is what they mean in practice.

### Be candid
Being candid means saying what you think, kindly but clearly. It means giving feedback that helps, rather than feedback that hurts, but it also means not hiding bad news. If you are behind on a project, say so early. If you think a client’s request is misguided, explain why before you do it. Candour saves us from surprises and ensures we solve the real problem, not just the easy one.

*Example:* A junior analyst notices that a model the team is building will not scale for the client’s data volume. Instead of staying quiet because they feel inexperienced, they speak up during the planning meeting, offering a simpler alternative that achieves 90% of the result in half the time. The team appreciates the honesty and adjusts the scope.

### Own the outcome
We are a consultancy, which means our people are trusted to deliver results without being micromanaged. Owning the outcome means taking responsibility for your work from start to finish. It means you don’t stop at "I sent the email" or "I handed it off." You check that the job is actually done and that it worked. If you hit a blocker, you find a way around it or ask for help explicitly. You are accountable for the result, not just the activity.

*Example:* A consultant is asked to prepare a report for a client. They send the draft, but then realize the formatting is broken in the PDF export. Instead of leaving it to the project manager to notice, they fix it, re-export, and confirm the client received a clean file. The consultant owns the final quality of the deliverable.

### Make it simple
Data is complex; our work doesn’t have to be. We aim for clarity in our code, our presentations, and our processes. If a process takes three steps but could take one, find the way to do it in one. If a report has ten charts but the insight fits in one, cut the other nine. Simplicity reduces errors, saves time, and makes our work easier for everyone to understand and maintain.

*Example:* The team has been using a complicated spreadsheet for tracking project hours. A developer builds a simple script that pulls the same data from our time-tracking tool and puts it in a dashboard. The new method takes ten minutes a week instead of two hours, and nobody makes copy-paste errors anymore.

### Leave room for others
We work in a collaborative environment, even when we are working remotely. Leaving room for others means being considerate of your colleagues’ time, space, and contributions. It means listening before you speak, sharing credit, and not dominating meetings. It also means creating space for different perspectives, especially those that differ from your own.

*Example:* During a brainstorming session, one team member jumps in with a solution immediately. A more senior colleague pauses and asks, "Does anyone else have an angle we haven’t tried yet?" This gives the quieter analyst the room to suggest a method that ends up being the key to the problem.

We believe these values make Harbourlight a better place to work and a better partner for our clients. We expect every employee, from new starters to senior leadership, to bring these values into their daily work.

Who to ask: Your manager

## 2. How We Work

Our work is project-based and client-focused, which means the rhythm of our weeks can vary. However, we have some consistent structures to help us stay aligned without being tied to a desk. We believe in flexibility as long as the work gets done and the team stays connected.

### Working Hours
Your standard working week is 37.5 hours. We do not track your time minute-by-minute, but we do expect you to manage your workload effectively.

We have **core hours from 10:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday**. During these six hours, you are expected to be available and online (whether you are in the office or working from home). Outside of core hours, you arrange your own day. If you prefer to start early and finish early, or to start later and finish later, that is fine, as long as you are covering your core hours and meeting your deadlines.

### Daily Stand-ups
We start our day together. Team stand-ups happen at **10:15**, just after core hours begin. These are short (15 minutes max) syncs where you briefly say what you did yesterday, what you are doing today, and if you are blocked by anything. It is not a status report to your manager; it is a way for the team to spot each other’s bottlenecks and offer help early.

If you are working from home, join via our video platform. If you are in the office, meet in the designated zone. The goal is connection, not surveillance.

### Communication
We keep our digital footprint simple to avoid noise. We use **one primary chat tool** for daily communication and **one shared calendar** for scheduling. 

- **Chat (Slack/Teams equivalent):** Use this for questions, updates, and informal conversation. It is asynchronous; people will not answer instantly, and that is okay. 
- **Email:** Use this for formal communication with clients, external stakeholders, or when you need a documented thread that can be forwarded.
- **Phone:** Use this for **urgent** requests or sensitive conversations. If something is truly urgent (e.g., a server is down, a client is angry right now), call or SMS. Do not rely on chat for emergencies.

### Office and Remote Work
We are a hybrid team. Some people are in the office most days, some work from home mostly, and some split the week. **We treat everyone equally regardless of location.** What matters is your output and your collaboration, not your physical presence. 

If you are working from home, it is your responsibility to create an environment where you can focus and where your audio/video is professional. If you are in the office, be mindful of others’ focus time. Headphones are a great signal that you are in deep work mode.

We do not require you to be online 24/7. We encourage you to respect your own boundaries and the boundaries of your colleagues. If you finish at 17:00, you do not need to answer chat messages at 21:00 unless you choose to. 

Who to ask: Your manager

## 3. Employment Basics

This chapter covers the administrative details of your employment with us. Please read this carefully and keep it handy, as it contains important numbers and deadlines that affect your contract and pay.

### Probation Period
Every new starter has a **3-month probation period**. This is a two-way street: we want to see if you are a good fit for the team, and you want to see if we are the right place for you.

During probation, you will have a **formal check-in at the end of each month** (month 1, month 2, and month 3). These meetings are with your manager. They are a chance to give and get feedback, clear up any confusion about your role, and adjust expectations if needed. 

If everything is going well, you will be confirmed as a permanent employee at the end of month 3. If there are issues, your manager will document them and provide a support plan. In some cases, probation may be extended by up to 3 months, but this decision is made transparently and with clear reasons.

### Notice Periods
When you want to leave, or if we need to end your employment, there is a notice period. 

- **During Probation:** The notice period is **1 week** for both you and the company. 
- **After Probation:** The notice period is **4 weeks** for both you and the company. 

This notice period applies whether you are resigning voluntarily or if the company is initiating termination. We expect you to serve this notice unless we agree otherwise in writing (e.g., paying you out).

### Contract Type
Unless your offer letter explicitly states a fixed-term contract, your contract with Harbourlight Analytics is **permanent**. There are no hidden probation extensions or auto-terminations. Your role continues indefinitely until one of you gives notice.

### Personal Details and Updates
We need accurate information for payroll, tax, and emergency contacts. If your personal details change, you must update them **within 2 weeks**.

Changes that must be reported to People Operations include:
- Change of home address
- Change of phone number
- Change of bank account details (for payroll)
- Change in emergency contact details
- Change in marital status or name

You can update most of these in our HR portal. If you are unsure where to go, email People Operations directly. Do not wait for the next payroll cycle; late updates can result in delayed payments or incorrect tax coding.

### Probation and Performance
The probation period is not just a waiting room; it is an active evaluation. Your manager will be looking for evidence of your values in action. Are you being candid? Are you owning your outcomes? Are you making work simple? 

If you are struggling, say so. We prefer to coach you through it than to let you fail quietly. If you are excelling, your manager should be recognizing that too. The monthly check-ins are your safety net—use them.

Who to ask: People Operations

## Pay and Benefits

## 4. Pay and Benefits

We want you to feel secure in your financial stability so you can focus on doing your best work. Here is how we handle pay and the benefits that come with it.

### Salaries
Your salary is paid monthly, on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or a public holiday, we pay on the last working day before it. You will receive an electronic payslip along with your payment, which breaks down your gross pay, deductions, and net pay. If you notice any errors on your payslip, please contact Finance immediately so we can correct them in the next cycle.

### Salary Reviews
We believe in fair pay and transparency. Our salary bands are reviewed every April. During this review, we look at market data, your role, and your performance to ensure your compensation remains competitive. If your role or responsibilities change significantly outside of this cycle, your manager may discuss a review with you, but the standard annual review is the primary time for adjustments.

### Benefits
We offer a package of benefits designed to support your health, your growth, and your lifestyle.

*   **Learning Budget:** You have a personal learning budget of €1,200 per year. This can be used for conferences, online courses, books, or workshops that help you develop your skills. You don't need to ask for permission for most things under this budget, but it is good practice to let your manager know what you are learning so they can support you.
*   **Home-Office Allowance:** If you are a new starter, you receive a one-off home-office allowance of €500. You can use this to buy a desk, chair, monitor, or other equipment to make your workspace comfortable. Submit your receipts to Finance for reimbursement.
*   **Health Insurance:** You are covered by our private health insurance plan from day one. You do not need to wait for a probation period to end. We will send you the details on how to activate your card and access providers.
*   **Pension:** We care about your future. We contribute 6% of your salary to your pension. To keep this match, you must contribute at least 3% of your salary. We handle the paperwork, but you should check your pension statement annually to make sure it aligns with your goals.
*   **Cycle-to-Work Scheme:** If you prefer to commute by bike, we offer a cycle-to-work scheme. This allows you to rent a bike and safety equipment through salary sacrifice, which can save you money on tax and national insurance.

Who to ask: Finance for payroll questions, People Operations for benefits queries.

## 5. Leave and Time Off

Rest is productive. We want you to take your breaks and use your leave to recharge, handle life events, and stay healthy. Here are the seven types of leave we offer.

### Annual Leave
You are entitled to 25 days of annual leave per year, plus 8 public holidays. This gives you plenty of time to switch off.

*   **Carryover:** If you have unused days at the end of the year, you can carry over up to 5 days. These carried-over days must be used by 31 March of the following year. Any remaining carried-over days after this date are forfeited.
*   **Booking:** You must give at least 2 weeks' notice for annual leave longer than 3 consecutive days. For shorter breaks, try to give as much notice as possible so we can plan coverage.

### Sick Leave
If you are unwell, please let your manager know as soon as you can. We provide 10 days of sick leave per year on full pay. If your absence lasts 5 consecutive days or more, we require a doctor's note (also known as a fit note) to document the absence. For shorter absences, we trust you to report your status honestly.

### Parental Leave
We support new parents fully.
*   **Primary Carer:** You are entitled to 16 weeks of parental leave on full pay.
*   **Partner Leave:** Your partner is entitled to 4 weeks of leave on full pay. This leave must be taken within the first 6 months of the child's birth or placement.

### Bereavement Leave
We offer compassionate support when you lose someone close to you.
*   **Standard:** 3 days of paid leave for the loss of a friend, relative, or close colleague.
*   **Immediate Family:** 5 days of paid leave for the loss of a partner, child, or parent.

### Jury and Public Duty Leave
If you are called for jury service or public duty (such as serving as a magistrate), you are entitled to paid leave for as long as the duty lasts. Please provide the court or official body's paperwork to People Operations so we can adjust your schedule and ensure you continue to receive your full salary during this time.

### Unpaid Leave
Sometimes, you may need extended time off that doesn't fall into the other categories. We can agree to up to 20 days of unpaid leave per year. This must be discussed and agreed upon with your manager in advance, and it will be documented in writing.

### Summary of Leave Types

| Leave Type | Entitlement | How to Request It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Annual Leave | 25 days + 8 public holidays | Submit request in shared calendar 2+ weeks in advance for >3 days |
| Sick Leave | 10 days per year (full pay) | Inform manager as soon as possible; provide note after 5 consecutive days |
| Parental Leave (Primary) | 16 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager as soon as date is known |
| Partner Leave | 4 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager; must be taken within first 6 months |
| Bereavement Leave | 3 days (standard) / 5 days (immediate family) | Inform manager immediately; follow up with HR if extended |
| Jury/Public Duty | Full salary for duration | Provide court/official paperwork to People Operations |
| Unpaid Leave | Up to 20 days per year | Discuss and agree with manager in advance |

Who to ask: Your manager for approval and People Operations for policy questions or documentation.

## Health, Safety, Equipment and Conduct

## Health, Safety and Wellbeing

We want you to stay healthy and safe while doing your work, whether that means sitting at a desk in our office or working from your kitchen table. This isn't just about avoiding accidents; it's about creating an environment where you can sustain good performance without burning out.

**First Aid and Emergencies**
In our office, we have trained first-aiders available to help if someone gets injured or falls ill. You can find the current list of trained first-aiders on the office noticeboard near the main entrance. If you are working remotely, please ensure you know the location of the nearest medical facility and have emergency contacts saved on your phone.

In case of a fire or serious emergency, follow the evacuation routes posted in the office. If you are working from home, have a basic emergency plan for your household.

**Employee Assistance Line**
Life can get complicated, and sometimes work stress or personal issues can impact your wellbeing. Everyone at Harbourlight has access to our confidential employee assistance line. This service is free for you to use, at any time, for any reason. You don't need to tell your manager or us about using it; it is completely private. You can call them to talk through anything, from relationship stress to financial worries or just needing a neutral ear.

**Home Worker Safety**
If you work mostly or entirely from home, your health and safety at your desk matters to us. During your first month, you are asked to complete a short workstation self-assessment. This helps you spot potential issues like poor posture or bad lighting before they become problems. Your manager will send you a link to this assessment. It’s not a test, and there’s no pass or fail; it’s just a tool to help you set up your space safely.

Who to ask: People Operations

## Equipment, Security and Data

We trust you with our tools because we trust you with our work. However, data security is a team sport, and some rules are non-negotiable to keep both you and our clients safe.

**Company Laptops**
Everyone gets a company laptop. This is your primary work device, whether you are in the office or at home. To protect the data on it, two security settings are mandatory and enforced automatically:
1.  **Full-disk encryption:** Your entire drive is encrypted so that if the device is stolen, the data is unreadable.
2.  **Automatic screen lock:** Your screen will lock automatically after **5 minutes** of inactivity. You can adjust the timing if you are in a secure environment, but never leave the screen unlocked when you step away.

**Data Handling**
Client data is our most valuable asset, and our clients trust us to keep it secure. Therefore, **client data must stay on company systems**. Never copy client files, databases, or sensitive information to personal devices, personal cloud storage (like your personal Dropbox or Google Drive), or personal email accounts. If you need to access a file while on the go, use the secure company portal or virtual desktop.

**Lost or Stolen Equipment**
If your laptop is lost or stolen, time is critical. You must report it to IT **within 1 hour** of discovering it is missing. This allows us to remotely wipe the data or lock the account before anyone else can access it. Please use the emergency IT hotline or email IT immediately.

**Passwords and Access**
You must use our company-approved **password manager** for all work-related accounts. Do not use the same password for different accounts, and do not save passwords in your browser or a text file. The password manager ensures you have strong, unique passwords for every service without needing to remember them all.

Who to ask: IT

## Code of Conduct

Our values—*Be candid, Own the outcome, Make it simple, Leave room for others*—are the compass for our behavior. This chapter translates those values into the everyday commitments we make to each other and to our clients.

### Our Conduct Commitments

1.  **We act with integrity.** We do the right thing, even when no one is watching. We do not misrepresent facts, inflate results, or hide mistakes.
2.  **We communicate openly and honestly.** We speak up early if something is going wrong. We give feedback kindly but clearly, and we listen to receive feedback as a gift.
3.  **We respect confidentiality.** We protect the private information of our colleagues, clients, and partners. We understand that what is said in a meeting or shared in a document stays within the appropriate circle.
4.  **We treat others with respect.** We create an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or bullying of any kind.
5.  **We use company time and resources for business purposes.** We are accountable for how we spend our working hours. Side projects must be disclosed if they could create a conflict of interest.
6.  **We are responsible stewards of data.** We follow security protocols because we know that a single slip can harm many people. We report security incidents immediately.
7.  **We collaborate rather than compete internally.** We share credit. We help teammates who are stuck. We don't hoard information to gain leverage.
8.  **We represent Harbourlight professionally.** Whether in an email, on a call, or on social media, we remember that we carry the company's name. We are polite, punctual, and prepared.

### Raising a Concern

Sometimes you might see something that feels wrong. It might be a safety hazard, a potential conflict of interest, or a breach of our code of conduct. If you have a concern, please raise it. We want to know.

Here is how you can raise a concern:

*   **Talk to your manager:** If you feel comfortable, your manager is the first point of contact. They are trained to handle sensitive issues and will escalate if necessary.
*   **Contact People Operations:** You can go directly to People Operations. They will listen confidentially and guide you on the next steps.
*   **Use the anonymous reporting channel:** If you prefer not to share your identity, you can submit a report anonymously through our secure online portal. This is designed for serious concerns where you may fear retaliation or feel unable to speak directly to anyone at the company.

**No Retaliation**
We promise that **nobody will be penalised for raising a concern in good faith**. Even if it turns out that the concern was unfounded, if you raised it honestly and without malice, your job and your career here are safe. We will investigate all reports fairly and promptly, and we will keep your identity protected as much as possible.

Who to ask: People Operations

## Growth, Feedback and Reviews

# 9. Growth, Feedback and Reviews

At Harbourlight Analytics, we want you to grow. Not just in your technical skills, but in your confidence, your judgement, and your ability to lead. Growth doesn’t happen by accident; it happens through conversation, reflection, and intentional effort. Here is how we support that process.

## Monthly One-to-Ones

Your primary channel for ongoing feedback is your monthly one-to-one with your manager. This is not a status update. You can get status updates in stand-ups and project plans. This meeting is for you. It is a dedicated space to discuss what is going well, what is getting in your way, and where you want to go next.

You should come prepared. Think about:

- What you have achieved since the last meeting.
- Any blockers or challenges you are facing.
- What support you need from your manager or the wider team.
- One or two areas you would like to develop in the coming month.

Your manager will use this time to give you specific, actionable feedback on your recent work. We expect managers to be candid here. If something went poorly, we talk about it honestly. If something went well, we celebrate it clearly. The goal is to keep us aligned so there are no surprises at formal reviews.

## Formal Reviews: April and October

We conduct formal performance and development reviews twice a year: once in April and once in October. These reviews are a structured opportunity to step back from the day-to-day and look at the bigger picture.

Before the review, you will fill out a self-assessment. This asks you to reflect on your contributions over the last six months, your skills development, and your goals for the next six months. Your manager will also write an assessment. We will use both documents as the basis for our conversation.

During the review meeting, we will discuss:

- Your performance against your goals and our values.
- What strengths you have demonstrated.
- Areas where you want to grow.
- Your learning and development needs.
- Your career trajectory.

The outcome of the review is a written document agreed upon by you and your manager. This document should outline clear objectives for the next period and specific actions to support your development.

## Promotion Discussions

Promotions are not automatic, and they are not guaranteed. But they are a real possibility for everyone at Harbourlight. We want to be as transparent as possible about how promotions work.

Promotion discussions are held during the April review cycle. If you believe you are performing at the next level, or if you have already been doing so for some time, raise it in your self-assessment and discuss it with your manager in your April one-to-one or review. We look for consistent evidence that you are operating at the next level, not just a single big win. This evidence includes:

- The complexity and impact of the work you have delivered.
- Your ability to work independently and own outcomes.
- How you contribute to the team and our culture.
- Feedback from peers and clients.

If you are not ready for promotion, we will tell you exactly why and what you need to do to get there. We will create a development plan with clear milestones. If you are ready, we will begin the formal process, which includes gathering broader feedback and, if necessary, a presentation to our leadership team. The goal is to make these decisions fairly and consistently, based on clear criteria, not office politics.

## Learning and Development

You have a personal learning budget of €1,200 per year. Use it. Whether it is a conference, an online course, a book, or a workshop, we encourage you to invest in your own growth. If you want to attend a major conference or take a significant certification course, discuss it with your manager early in the year to ensure it fits your development plan and our business needs.

We also believe in learning from others. Take advantage of internal knowledge-sharing sessions, and consider volunteering to lead one. Teaching is one of the best ways to learn.

**Who to ask:** Your manager


# 10. Leaving Harbourlight

We hope you stay at Harbourlight Analytics for a long time. But we know that people’s lives and careers change, and that sometimes moving on is the right step. We want to make the exit process as smooth, respectful, and practical as possible for you.

## Resignation

If you decide to leave, please speak to your manager in person or on a call first. After that, submit your resignation in writing to People Operations. This ensures everyone is on the same page regarding your last day and allows us to start the transition planning.

## The Notice Period

Your notice period depends on your status:

- If you are still in your probation period, the notice period is 1 week.
- If you have completed probation, the notice period is 4 weeks.

During this time, your goal is to hand over your work cleanly. Work with your manager and team to document your responsibilities, introduce your replacement (if hired) or colleagues who will take over, and ensure client expectations are managed.

## Equipment and Access

You are responsible for the company equipment assigned to you. On your last day, you must return all company equipment to IT or People Operations. This includes:

- Your company laptop.
- Your company phone (if applicable).
- Any security keys, hardware tokens, or peripherals.
- Your office access card or keys.

We will also schedule a time to revoke your system access. Typically, this happens on your last day to ensure security. Before you leave, make sure all your work is saved on company systems and that you have not copied any client data or confidential information to personal devices. Please review Chapter 7 (Equipment, Security and Data) if you are unsure about what you can and cannot take with you.

## The Exit Conversation

We conduct an exit conversation with People Operations. This is not a formalities check. We genuinely want to know what you liked about working here, what you did not, and what we could do better. Your honest feedback helps us improve the experience for future employees. You are welcome to be candid. We will treat your comments with confidentiality and use them to inform our practices.

## Final Pay and Benefits

Your final salary payment will be made on the usual payday after your last day. 

- **Unused Annual Leave:** If you have accrued annual leave that you have not used, we will pay it out in your final salary. We calculate this based on your current daily rate.
- **Other Deductions:** If you have purchased anything via a salary sacrifice scheme (like a bike), we will settle those accounts before you leave.
- **Benefits:** Your private health insurance and pension contributions will stop on your last day of employment. We will provide you with the necessary information if you wish to transfer your pension or arrange private cover.

## References

We are happy to provide references for former employees. If you need a reference, ask your manager or People Operations. Please note that our standard reference policy is to confirm only your job title, your dates of employment, and your role. This is to ensure consistency and fairness for all employees. If you need a more detailed reference, you will need to ask a former colleague or manager directly, and they may choose to provide one, but it is not company policy to do so.

## After You Leave

We want to maintain good relationships. If you leave on good terms, you are welcome to stay connected. We will share occasional company updates with alumni, and we would love to hear about what you are doing next.

**Who to ask:** People Operations

## 1. Welcome and Our Values

Welcome to Harbourlight Analytics. You are joining a team of thirty data consultants who are passionate about helping clients see their data more clearly. We have grown from eight people to thirty in eighteen months, and while we have more faces around the office (and on video calls) than we did at the start, our culture hasn’t changed. We are a group of professionals who support each other, respect each other’s time, and take pride in doing good work.

We don’t have a rulebook for every human interaction, but we do have four values that guide how we treat each other and our clients. These aren’t just posters on a wall; they are the tools we use to make decisions when there isn’t a clear right answer. Here is what they mean in practice.

### Be candid
Being candid means saying what you think, kindly but clearly. It means giving feedback that helps, rather than feedback that hurts, but it also means not hiding bad news. If you are behind on a project, say so early. If you think a client’s request is misguided, explain why before you do it. Candour saves us from surprises and ensures we solve the real problem, not just the easy one.

*Example:* A junior analyst notices that a model the team is building will not scale for the client’s data volume. Instead of staying quiet because they feel inexperienced, they speak up during the planning meeting, offering a simpler alternative that achieves 90% of the result in half the time. The team appreciates the honesty and adjusts the scope.

### Own the outcome
We are a consultancy, which means our people are trusted to deliver results without being micromanaged. Owning the outcome means taking responsibility for your work from start to finish. It means you don’t stop at "I sent the email" or "I handed it off." You check that the job is actually done and that it worked. If you hit a blocker, you find a way around it or ask for help explicitly. You are accountable for the result, not just the activity.

*Example:* A consultant is asked to prepare a report for a client. They send the draft, but then realize the formatting is broken in the PDF export. Instead of leaving it to the project manager to notice, they fix it, re-export, and confirm the client received a clean file. The consultant owns the final quality of the deliverable.

### Make it simple
Data is complex; our work doesn’t have to be. We aim for clarity in our code, our presentations, and our processes. If a process takes three steps but could take one, find the way to do it in one. If a report has ten charts but the insight fits in one, cut the other nine. Simplicity reduces errors, saves time, and makes our work easier for everyone to understand and maintain.

*Example:* The team has been using a complicated spreadsheet for tracking project hours. A developer builds a simple script that pulls the same data from our time-tracking tool and puts it in a dashboard. The new method takes ten minutes a week instead of two hours, and nobody makes copy-paste errors anymore.

### Leave room for others
We work in a collaborative environment, even when we are working remotely. Leaving room for others means being considerate of your colleagues’ time, space, and contributions. It means listening before you speak, sharing credit, and not dominating meetings. It also means creating space for different perspectives, especially those that differ from your own.

*Example:* During a brainstorming session, one team member jumps in with a solution immediately. A more senior colleague pauses and asks, "Does anyone else have an angle we haven’t tried yet?" This gives the quieter analyst the room to suggest a method that ends up being the key to the problem.

We believe these values make Harbourlight a better place to work and a better partner for our clients. We expect every employee, from new starters to senior leadership, to bring these values into their daily work.

Who to ask: Your manager

## 2. How We Work

Our work is project-based and client-focused, which means the rhythm of our weeks can vary. However, we have some consistent structures to help us stay aligned without being tied to a desk. We believe in flexibility as long as the work gets done and the team stays connected.

### Working Hours
Your standard working week is 37.5 hours. We do not track your time minute-by-minute, but we do expect you to manage your workload effectively.

We have **core hours from 10:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday**. During these six hours, you are expected to be available and online (whether you are in the office or working from home). Outside of core hours, you arrange your own day. If you prefer to start early and finish early, or to start later and finish later, that is fine, as long as you are covering your core hours and meeting your deadlines.

### Daily Stand-ups
We start our day together. Team stand-ups happen at **10:15**, just after core hours begin. These are short (15 minutes max) syncs where you briefly say what you did yesterday, what you are doing today, and if you are blocked by anything. It is not a status report to your manager; it is a way for the team to spot each other’s bottlenecks and offer help early.

If you are working from home, join via our video platform. If you are in the office, meet in the designated zone. The goal is connection, not surveillance.

### Communication
We keep our digital footprint simple to avoid noise. We use **one primary chat tool** for daily communication and **one shared calendar** for scheduling. 

- **Chat (Slack/Teams equivalent):** Use this for questions, updates, and informal conversation. It is asynchronous; people will not answer instantly, and that is okay. 
- **Email:** Use this for formal communication with clients, external stakeholders, or when you need a documented thread that can be forwarded.
- **Phone:** Use this for **urgent** requests or sensitive conversations. If something is truly urgent (e.g., a server is down, a client is angry right now), call or SMS. Do not rely on chat for emergencies.

### Office and Remote Work
We are a hybrid team. Some people are in the office most days, some work from home mostly, and some split the week. **We treat everyone equally regardless of location.** What matters is your output and your collaboration, not your physical presence. 

If you are working from home, it is your responsibility to create an environment where you can focus and where your audio/video is professional. If you are in the office, be mindful of others’ focus time. Headphones are a great signal that you are in deep work mode.

We do not require you to be online 24/7. We encourage you to respect your own boundaries and the boundaries of your colleagues. If you finish at 17:00, you do not need to answer chat messages at 21:00 unless you choose to. 

Who to ask: Your manager

## 3. Employment Basics

This chapter covers the administrative details of your employment with us. Please read this carefully and keep it handy, as it contains important numbers and deadlines that affect your contract and pay.

### Probation Period
Every new starter has a **3-month probation period**. This is a two-way street: we want to see if you are a good fit for the team, and you want to see if we are the right place for you.

During probation, you will have a **formal check-in at the end of each month** (month 1, month 2, and month 3). These meetings are with your manager. They are a chance to give and get feedback, clear up any confusion about your role, and adjust expectations if needed. 

If everything is going well, you will be confirmed as a permanent employee at the end of month 3. If there are issues, your manager will document them and provide a support plan. In some cases, probation may be extended by up to 3 months, but this decision is made transparently and with clear reasons.

### Notice Periods
When you want to leave, or if we need to end your employment, there is a notice period. 

- **During Probation:** The notice period is **1 week** for both you and the company. 
- **After Probation:** The notice period is **4 weeks** for both you and the company. 

This notice period applies whether you are resigning voluntarily or if the company is initiating termination. We expect you to serve this notice unless we agree otherwise in writing (e.g., paying you out).

### Contract Type
Unless your offer letter explicitly states a fixed-term contract, your contract with Harbourlight Analytics is **permanent**. There are no hidden probation extensions or auto-terminations. Your role continues indefinitely until one of you gives notice.

### Personal Details and Updates
We need accurate information for payroll, tax, and emergency contacts. If your personal details change, you must update them **within 2 weeks**.

Changes that must be reported to People Operations include:
- Change of home address
- Change of phone number
- Change of bank account details (for payroll)
- Change in emergency contact details
- Change in marital status or name

You can update most of these in our HR portal. If you are unsure where to go, email People Operations directly. Do not wait for the next payroll cycle; late updates can result in delayed payments or incorrect tax coding.

### Probation and Performance
The probation period is not just a waiting room; it is an active evaluation. Your manager will be looking for evidence of your values in action. Are you being candid? Are you owning your outcomes? Are you making work simple? 

If you are struggling, say so. We prefer to coach you through it than to let you fail quietly. If you are excelling, your manager should be recognizing that too. The monthly check-ins are your safety net—use them.

Who to ask: People Operations

parts.title: Pay and Benefits
parts.body:
## 4. Pay and Benefits

We want you to feel secure in your financial stability so you can focus on doing your best work. Here is how we handle pay and the benefits that come with it.

### Salaries
Your salary is paid monthly, on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or a public holiday, we pay on the last working day before it. You will receive an electronic payslip along with your payment, which breaks down your gross pay, deductions, and net pay. If you notice any errors on your payslip, please contact Finance immediately so we can correct them in the next cycle.

### Salary Reviews
We believe in fair pay and transparency. Our salary bands are reviewed every April. During this review, we look at market data, your role, and your performance to ensure your compensation remains competitive. If your role or responsibilities change significantly outside of this cycle, your manager may discuss a review with you, but the standard annual review is the primary time for adjustments.

### Benefits
We offer a package of benefits designed to support your health, your growth, and your lifestyle.

*   **Learning Budget:** You have a personal learning budget of €1,200 per year. This can be used for conferences, online courses, books, or workshops that help you develop your skills. You don't need to ask for permission for most things under this budget, but it is good practice to let your manager know what you are learning so they can support you.
*   **Home-Office Allowance:** If you are a new starter, you receive a one-off home-office allowance of €500. You can use this to buy a desk, chair, monitor, or other equipment to make your workspace comfortable. Submit your receipts to Finance for reimbursement.
*   **Health Insurance:** You are covered by our private health insurance plan from day one. You do not need to wait for a probation period to end. We will send you the details on how to activate your card and access providers.
*   **Pension:** We care about your future. We contribute 6% of your salary to your pension. To keep this match, you must contribute at least 3% of your salary. We handle the paperwork, but you should check your pension statement annually to make sure it aligns with your goals.
*   **Cycle-to-Work Scheme:** If you prefer to commute by bike, we offer a cycle-to-work scheme. This allows you to rent a bike and safety equipment through salary sacrifice, which can save you money on tax and national insurance.

Who to ask: Finance for payroll questions, People Operations for benefits queries.

## 5. Leave and Time Off

Rest is productive. We want you to take your breaks and use your leave to recharge, handle life events, and stay healthy. Here are the seven types of leave we offer.

### Annual Leave
You are entitled to 25 days of annual leave per year, plus 8 public holidays. This gives you plenty of time to switch off.

*   **Carryover:** If you have unused days at the end of the year, you can carry over up to 5 days. These carried-over days must be used by 31 March of the following year. Any remaining carried-over days after this date are forfeited.
*   **Booking:** You must give at least 2 weeks' notice for annual leave longer than 3 consecutive days. For shorter breaks, try to give as much notice as possible so we can plan coverage.

### Sick Leave
If you are unwell, please let your manager know as soon as you can. We provide 10 days of sick leave per year on full pay. If your absence lasts 5 consecutive days or more, we require a doctor's note (also known as a fit note) to document the absence. For shorter absences, we trust you to report your status honestly.

### Parental Leave
We support new parents fully.
*   **Primary Carer:** You are entitled to 16 weeks of parental leave on full pay.
*   **Partner Leave:** Your partner is entitled to 4 weeks of leave on full pay. This leave must be taken within the first 6 months of the child's birth or placement.

### Bereavement Leave
We offer compassionate support when you lose someone close to you.
*   **Standard:** 3 days of paid leave for the loss of a friend, relative, or close colleague.
*   **Immediate Family:** 5 days of paid leave for the loss of a partner, child, or parent.

### Jury and Public Duty Leave
If you are called for jury service or public duty (such as serving as a magistrate), you are entitled to paid leave for as long as the duty lasts. Please provide the court or official body's paperwork to People Operations so we can adjust your schedule and ensure you continue to receive your full salary during this time.

### Unpaid Leave
Sometimes, you may need extended time off that doesn't fall into the other categories. We can agree to up to 20 days of unpaid leave per year. This must be discussed and agreed upon with your manager in advance, and it will be documented in writing.

### Summary of Leave Types

| Leave Type | Entitlement | How to Request It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Annual Leave | 25 days + 8 public holidays | Submit request in shared calendar 2+ weeks in advance for >3 days |
| Sick Leave | 10 days per year (full pay) | Inform manager as soon as possible; provide note after 5 consecutive days |
| Parental Leave (Primary) | 16 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager as soon as date is known |
| Partner Leave | 4 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager; must be taken within first 6 months |
| Bereavement Leave | 3 days (standard) / 5 days (immediate family) | Inform manager immediately; follow up with HR if extended |
| Jury/Public Duty | Full salary for duration | Provide court/official paperwork to People Operations |
| Unpaid Leave | Up to 20 days per year | Discuss and agree with manager in advance |

Who to ask: Your manager for approval and People Operations for policy questions or documentation.

parts.title: Health, Safety, Equipment and Conduct
parts.body:
## Health, Safety and Wellbeing

We want you to stay healthy and safe while doing your work, whether that means sitting at a desk in our office or working from your kitchen table. This isn't just about avoiding accidents; it's about creating an environment where you can sustain good performance without burning out.

**First Aid and Emergencies**
In our office, we have trained first-aiders available to help if someone gets injured or falls ill. You can find the current list of trained first-aiders on the office noticeboard near the main entrance. If you are working remotely, please ensure you know the location of the nearest medical facility and have emergency contacts saved on your phone.

In case of a fire or serious emergency, follow the evacuation routes posted in the office. If you are working from home, have a basic emergency plan for your household.

**Employee Assistance Line**
Life can get complicated, and sometimes work stress or personal issues can impact your wellbeing. Everyone at Harbourlight has access to our confidential employee assistance line. This service is free for you to use, at any time, for any reason. You don't need to tell your manager or us about using it; it is completely private. You can call them to talk through anything, from relationship stress to financial worries or just needing a neutral ear.

**Home Worker Safety**
If you work mostly or entirely from home, your health and safety at your desk matters to us. During your first month, you are asked to complete a short workstation self-assessment. This helps you spot potential issues like poor posture or bad lighting before they become problems. Your manager will send you a link to this assessment. It’s not a test, and there’s no pass or fail; it’s just a tool to help you set up your space safely.

Who to ask: People Operations

## Equipment, Security and Data

We trust you with our tools because we trust you with our work. However, data security is a team sport, and some rules are non-negotiable to keep both you and our clients safe.

**Company Laptops**
Everyone gets a company laptop. This is your primary work device, whether you are in the office or at home. To protect the data on it, two security settings are mandatory and enforced automatically:
1.  **Full-disk encryption:** Your entire drive is encrypted so that if the device is stolen, the data is unreadable.
2.  **Automatic screen lock:** Your screen will lock automatically after **5 minutes** of inactivity. You can adjust the timing if you are in a secure environment, but never leave the screen unlocked when you step away.

**Data Handling**
Client data is our most valuable asset, and our clients trust us to keep it secure. Therefore, **client data must stay on company systems**. Never copy client files, databases, or sensitive information to personal devices, personal cloud storage (like your personal Dropbox or Google Drive), or personal email accounts. If you need to access a file while on the go, use the secure company portal or virtual desktop.

**Lost or Stolen Equipment**
If your laptop is lost or stolen, time is critical. You must report it to IT **within 1 hour** of discovering it is missing. This allows us to remotely wipe the data or lock the account before anyone else can access it. Please use the emergency IT hotline or email IT immediately.

**Passwords and Access**
You must use our company-approved **password manager** for all work-related accounts. Do not use the same password for different accounts, and do not save passwords in your browser or a text file. The password manager ensures you have strong, unique passwords for every service without needing to remember them all.

Who to ask: IT

## Code of Conduct

Our values—*Be candid, Own the outcome, Make it simple, Leave room for others*—are the compass for our behavior. This chapter translates those values into the everyday commitments we make to each other and to our clients.

### Our Conduct Commitments

1.  **We act with integrity.** We do the right thing, even when no one is watching. We do not misrepresent facts, inflate results, or hide mistakes.
2.  **We communicate openly and honestly.** We speak up early if something is going wrong. We give feedback kindly but clearly, and we listen to receive feedback as a gift.
3.  **We respect confidentiality.** We protect the private information of our colleagues, clients, and partners. We understand that what is said in a meeting or shared in a document stays within the appropriate circle.
4.  **We treat others with respect.** We create an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or bullying of any kind.
5.  **We use company time and resources for business purposes.** We are accountable for how we spend our working hours. Side projects must be disclosed if they could create a conflict of interest.
6.  **We are responsible stewards of data.** We follow security protocols because we know that a single slip can harm many people. We report security incidents immediately.
7.  **We collaborate rather than compete internally.** We share credit. We help teammates who are stuck. We don't hoard information to gain leverage.
8.  **We represent Harbourlight professionally.** Whether in an email, on a call, or on social media, we remember that we carry the company's name. We are polite, punctual, and prepared.

### Raising a Concern

Sometimes you might see something that feels wrong. It might be a safety hazard, a potential conflict of interest, or a breach of our code of conduct. If you have a concern, please raise it. We want to know.

Here is how you can raise a concern:

*   **Talk to your manager:** If you feel comfortable, your manager is the first point of contact. They are trained to handle sensitive issues and will escalate if necessary.
*   **Contact People Operations:** You can go directly to People Operations. They will listen confidentially and guide you on the next steps.
*   **Use the anonymous reporting channel:** If you prefer not to share your identity, you can submit a report anonymously through our secure online portal. This is designed for serious concerns where you may fear retaliation or feel unable to speak directly to anyone at the company.

**No Retaliation**
We promise that **nobody will be penalised for raising a concern in good faith**. Even if it turns out that the concern was unfounded, if you raised it honestly and without malice, your job and your career here are safe. We will investigate all reports fairly and promptly, and we will keep your identity protected as much as possible.

Who to ask: People Operations

parts.title: Growth, Feedback and Reviews
parts.body:
# 9. Growth, Feedback and Reviews

At Harbourlight Analytics, we want you to grow. Not just in your technical skills, but in your confidence, your judgement, and your ability to lead. Growth doesn’t happen by accident; it happens through conversation, reflection, and intentional effort. Here is how we support that process.

## Monthly One-to-Ones

Your primary channel for ongoing feedback is your monthly one-to-one with your manager. This is not a status update. You can get status updates in stand-ups and project plans. This meeting is for you. It is a dedicated space to discuss what is going well, what is getting in your way, and where you want to go next.

You should come prepared. Think about:

- What you have achieved since the last meeting.
- Any blockers or challenges you are facing.
- What support you need from your manager or the wider team.
- One or two areas you would like to develop in the coming month.

Your manager will use this time to give you specific, actionable feedback on your recent work. We expect managers to be candid here. If something went poorly, we talk about it honestly. If something went well, we celebrate it clearly. The goal is to keep us aligned so there are no surprises at formal reviews.

## Formal Reviews: April and October

We conduct formal performance and development reviews twice a year: once in April and once in October. These reviews are a structured opportunity to step back from the day-to-day and look at the bigger picture.

Before the review, you will fill out a self-assessment. This asks you to reflect on your contributions over the last six months, your skills development, and your goals for the next six months. Your manager will also write an assessment. We will use both documents as the basis for our conversation.

During the review meeting, we will discuss:

- Your performance against your goals and our values.
- What strengths you have demonstrated.
- Areas where you want to grow.
- Your learning and development needs.
- Your career trajectory.

The outcome of the review is a written document agreed upon by you and your manager. This document should outline clear objectives for the next period and specific actions to support your development.

## Promotion Discussions

Promotions are not automatic, and they are not guaranteed. But they are a real possibility for everyone at Harbourlight. We want to be as transparent as possible about how promotions work.

Promotion discussions are held during the April review cycle. If you believe you are performing at the next level, or if you have already been doing so for some time, raise it in your self-assessment and discuss it with your manager in your April one-to-one or review. We look for consistent evidence that you are operating at the next level, not just a single big win. This evidence includes:

- The complexity and impact of the work you have delivered.
- Your ability to work independently and own outcomes.
- How you contribute to the team and our culture.
- Feedback from peers and clients.

If you are not ready for promotion, we will tell you exactly why and what you need to do to get there. We will create a development plan with clear milestones. If you are ready, we will begin the formal process, which includes gathering broader feedback and, if necessary, a presentation to our leadership team. The goal is to make these decisions fairly and consistently, based on clear criteria, not office politics.

## Learning and Development

You have a personal learning budget of €1,200 per year. Use it. Whether it is a conference, an online course, a book, or a workshop, we encourage you to invest in your own growth. If you want to attend a major conference or take a significant certification course, discuss it with your manager early in the year to ensure it fits your development plan and our business needs.

We also believe in learning from others. Take advantage of internal knowledge-sharing sessions, and consider volunteering to lead one. Teaching is one of the best ways to learn.

**Who to ask:** Your manager


# 10. Leaving Harbourlight

We hope you stay at Harbourlight Analytics for a long time. But we know that people’s lives and careers change, and that sometimes moving on is the right step. We want to make the exit process as smooth, respectful, and practical as possible for you.

## Resignation

If you decide to leave, please speak to your manager in person or on a call first. After that, submit your resignation in writing to People Operations. This ensures everyone is on the same page regarding your last day and allows us to start the transition planning.

## The Notice Period

Your notice period depends on your status:

- If you are still in your probation period, the notice period is 1 week.
- If you have completed probation, the notice period is 4 weeks.

During this time, your goal is to hand over your work cleanly. Work with your manager and team to document your responsibilities, introduce your replacement (if hired) or colleagues who will take over, and ensure client expectations are managed.

## Equipment and Access

You are responsible for the company equipment assigned to you. On your last day, you must return all company equipment to IT or People Operations. This includes:

- Your company laptop.
- Your company phone (if applicable).
- Any security keys, hardware tokens, or peripherals.
- Your office access card or keys.

We will also schedule a time to revoke your system access. Typically, this happens on your last day to ensure security. Before you leave, make sure all your work is saved on company systems and that you have not copied any client data or confidential information to personal devices. Please review Chapter 7 (Equipment, Security and Data) if you are unsure about what you can and cannot take with you.

## The Exit Conversation

We conduct an exit conversation with People Operations. This is not a formalities check. We genuinely want to know what you liked about working here, what you did not, and what we could do better. Your honest feedback helps us improve the experience for future employees. You are welcome to be candid. We will treat your comments with confidentiality and use them to inform our practices.

## Final Pay and Benefits

Your final salary payment will be made on the usual payday after your last day. 

- **Unused Annual Leave:** If you have accrued annual leave that you have not used, we will pay it out in your final salary. We calculate this based on your current daily rate.
- **Other Deductions:** If you have purchased anything via a salary sacrifice scheme (like a bike), we will settle those accounts before you leave.
- **Benefits:** Your private health insurance and pension contributions will stop on your last day of employment. We will provide you with the necessary information if you wish to transfer your pension or arrange private cover.

## References

We are happy to provide references for former employees. If you need a reference, ask your manager or People Operations. Please note that our standard reference policy is to confirm only your job title, your dates of employment, and your role. This is to ensure consistency and fairness for all employees. If you need a more detailed reference, you will need to ask a former colleague or manager directly, and they may choose to provide one, but it is not company policy to do so.

## After You Leave

We want to maintain good relationships. If you leave on good terms, you are welcome to stay connected. We will share occasional company updates with alumni, and we would love to hear about what you are doing next.

**Who to ask:** People Operations

## 1. Welcome and Our Values

Welcome to Harbourlight Analytics. You are joining a team of thirty data consultants who are passionate about helping clients see their data more clearly. We have grown from eight people to thirty in eighteen months, and while we have more faces around the office (and on video calls) than we did at the start, our culture hasn’t changed. We are a group of professionals who support each other, respect each other’s time, and take pride in doing good work.

We don’t have a rulebook for every human interaction, but we do have four values that guide how we treat each other and our clients. These aren’t just posters on a wall; they are the tools we use to make decisions when there isn’t a clear right answer. Here is what they mean in practice.

### Be candid
Being candid means saying what you think, kindly but clearly. It means giving feedback that helps, rather than feedback that hurts, but it also means not hiding bad news. If you are behind on a project, say so early. If you think a client’s request is misguided, explain why before you do it. Candour saves us from surprises and ensures we solve the real problem, not just the easy one.

*Example:* A junior analyst notices that a model the team is building will not scale for the client’s data volume. Instead of staying quiet because they feel inexperienced, they speak up during the planning meeting, offering a simpler alternative that achieves 90% of the result in half the time. The team appreciates the honesty and adjusts the scope.

### Own the outcome
We are a consultancy, which means our people are trusted to deliver results without being micromanaged. Owning the outcome means taking responsibility for your work from start to finish. It means you don’t stop at "I sent the email" or "I handed it off." You check that the job is actually done and that it worked. If you hit a blocker, you find a way around it or ask for help explicitly. You are accountable for the result, not just the activity.

*Example:* A consultant is asked to prepare a report for a client. They send the draft, but then realize the formatting is broken in the PDF export. Instead of leaving it to the project manager to notice, they fix it, re-export, and confirm the client received a clean file. The consultant owns the final quality of the deliverable.

### Make it simple
Data is complex; our work doesn’t have to be. We aim for clarity in our code, our presentations, and our processes. If a process takes three steps but could take one, find the way to do it in one. If a report has ten charts but the insight fits in one, cut the other nine. Simplicity reduces errors, saves time, and makes our work easier for everyone to understand and maintain.

*Example:* The team has been using a complicated spreadsheet for tracking project hours. A developer builds a simple script that pulls the same data from our time-tracking tool and puts it in a dashboard. The new method takes ten minutes a week instead of two hours, and nobody makes copy-paste errors anymore.

### Leave room for others
We work in a collaborative environment, even when we are working remotely. Leaving room for others means being considerate of your colleagues’ time, space, and contributions. It means listening before you speak, sharing credit, and not dominating meetings. It also means creating space for different perspectives, especially those that differ from your own.

*Example:* During a brainstorming session, one team member jumps in with a solution immediately. A more senior colleague pauses and asks, "Does anyone else have an angle we haven’t tried yet?" This gives the quieter analyst the room to suggest a method that ends up being the key to the problem.

We believe these values make Harbourlight a better place to work and a better partner for our clients. We expect every employee, from new starters to senior leadership, to bring these values into their daily work.

Who to ask: Your manager

## 2. How We Work

Our work is project-based and client-focused, which means the rhythm of our weeks can vary. However, we have some consistent structures to help us stay aligned without being tied to a desk. We believe in flexibility as long as the work gets done and the team stays connected.

### Working Hours
Your standard working week is 37.5 hours. We do not track your time minute-by-minute, but we do expect you to manage your workload effectively.

We have **core hours from 10:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday**. During these six hours, you are expected to be available and online (whether you are in the office or working from home). Outside of core hours, you arrange your own day. If you prefer to start early and finish early, or to start later and finish later, that is fine, as long as you are covering your core hours and meeting your deadlines.

### Daily Stand-ups
We start our day together. Team stand-ups happen at **10:15**, just after core hours begin. These are short (15 minutes max) syncs where you briefly say what you did yesterday, what you are doing today, and if you are blocked by anything. It is not a status report to your manager; it is a way for the team to spot each other’s bottlenecks and offer help early.

If you are working from home, join via our video platform. If you are in the office, meet in the designated zone. The goal is connection, not surveillance.

### Communication
We keep our digital footprint simple to avoid noise. We use **one primary chat tool** for daily communication and **one shared calendar** for scheduling. 

- **Chat (Slack/Teams equivalent):** Use this for questions, updates, and informal conversation. It is asynchronous; people will not answer instantly, and that is okay. 
- **Email:** Use this for formal communication with clients, external stakeholders, or when you need a documented thread that can be forwarded.
- **Phone:** Use this for **urgent** requests or sensitive conversations. If something is truly urgent (e.g., a server is down, a client is angry right now), call or SMS. Do not rely on chat for emergencies.

### Office and Remote Work
We are a hybrid team. Some people are in the office most days, some work from home mostly, and some split the week. **We treat everyone equally regardless of location.** What matters is your output and your collaboration, not your physical presence. 

If you are working from home, it is your responsibility to create an environment where you can focus and where your audio/video is professional. If you are in the office, be mindful of others’ focus time. Headphones are a great signal that you are in deep work mode.

We do not require you to be online 24/7. We encourage you to respect your own boundaries and the boundaries of your colleagues. If you finish at 17:00, you do not need to answer chat messages at 21:00 unless you choose to. 

Who to ask: Your manager

## 3. Employment Basics

This chapter covers the administrative details of your employment with us. Please read this carefully and keep it handy, as it contains important numbers and deadlines that affect your contract and pay.

### Probation Period
Every new starter has a **3-month probation period**. This is a two-way street: we want to see if you are a good fit for the team, and you want to see if we are the right place for you.

During probation, you will have a **formal check-in at the end of each month** (month 1, month 2, and month 3). These meetings are with your manager. They are a chance to give and get feedback, clear up any confusion about your role, and adjust expectations if needed. 

If everything is going well, you will be confirmed as a permanent employee at the end of month 3. If there are issues, your manager will document them and provide a support plan. In some cases, probation may be extended by up to 3 months, but this decision is made transparently and with clear reasons.

### Notice Periods
When you want to leave, or if we need to end your employment, there is a notice period. 

- **During Probation:** The notice period is **1 week** for both you and the company. 
- **After Probation:** The notice period is **4 weeks** for both you and the company. 

This notice period applies whether you are resigning voluntarily or if the company is initiating termination. We expect you to serve this notice unless we agree otherwise in writing (e.g., paying you out).

### Contract Type
Unless your offer letter explicitly states a fixed-term contract, your contract with Harbourlight Analytics is **permanent**. There are no hidden probation extensions or auto-terminations. Your role continues indefinitely until one of you gives notice.

### Personal Details and Updates
We need accurate information for payroll, tax, and emergency contacts. If your personal details change, you must update them **within 2 weeks**.

Changes that must be reported to People Operations include:
- Change of home address
- Change of phone number
- Change of bank account details (for payroll)
- Change in emergency contact details
- Change in marital status or name

You can update most of these in our HR portal. If you are unsure where to go, email People Operations directly. Do not wait for the next payroll cycle; late updates can result in delayed payments or incorrect tax coding.

### Probation and Performance
The probation period is not just a waiting room; it is an active evaluation. Your manager will be looking for evidence of your values in action. Are you being candid? Are you owning your outcomes? Are you making work simple? 

If you are struggling, say so. We prefer to coach you through it than to let you fail quietly. If you are excelling, your manager should be recognizing that too. The monthly check-ins are your safety net—use them.

Who to ask: People Operations

## Pay and Benefits

## 4. Pay and Benefits

We want you to feel secure in your financial stability so you can focus on doing your best work. Here is how we handle pay and the benefits that come with it.

### Salaries
Your salary is paid monthly, on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or a public holiday, we pay on the last working day before it. You will receive an electronic payslip along with your payment, which breaks down your gross pay, deductions, and net pay. If you notice any errors on your payslip, please contact Finance immediately so we can correct them in the next cycle.

### Salary Reviews
We believe in fair pay and transparency. Our salary bands are reviewed every April. During this review, we look at market data, your role, and your performance to ensure your compensation remains competitive. If your role or responsibilities change significantly outside of this cycle, your manager may discuss a review with you, but the standard annual review is the primary time for adjustments.

### Benefits
We offer a package of benefits designed to support your health, your growth, and your lifestyle.

*   **Learning Budget:** You have a personal learning budget of €1,200 per year. This can be used for conferences, online courses, books, or workshops that help you develop your skills. You don't need to ask for permission for most things under this budget, but it is good practice to let your manager know what you are learning so they can support you.
*   **Home-Office Allowance:** If you are a new starter, you receive a one-off home-office allowance of €500. You can use this to buy a desk, chair, monitor, or other equipment to make your workspace comfortable. Submit your receipts to Finance for reimbursement.
*   **Health Insurance:** You are covered by our private health insurance plan from day one. You do not need to wait for a probation period to end. We will send you the details on how to activate your card and access providers.
*   **Pension:** We care about your future. We contribute 6% of your salary to your pension. To keep this match, you must contribute at least 3% of your salary. We handle the paperwork, but you should check your pension statement annually to make sure it aligns with your goals.
*   **Cycle-to-Work Scheme:** If you prefer to commute by bike, we offer a cycle-to-work scheme. This allows you to rent a bike and safety equipment through salary sacrifice, which can save you money on tax and national insurance.

Who to ask: Finance for payroll questions, People Operations for benefits queries.

## 5. Leave and Time Off

Rest is productive. We want you to take your breaks and use your leave to recharge, handle life events, and stay healthy. Here are the seven types of leave we offer.

### Annual Leave
You are entitled to 25 days of annual leave per year, plus 8 public holidays. This gives you plenty of time to switch off.

*   **Carryover:** If you have unused days at the end of the year, you can carry over up to 5 days. These carried-over days must be used by 31 March of the following year. Any remaining carried-over days after this date are forfeited.
*   **Booking:** You must give at least 2 weeks' notice for annual leave longer than 3 consecutive days. For shorter breaks, try to give as much notice as possible so we can plan coverage.

### Sick Leave
If you are unwell, please let your manager know as soon as you can. We provide 10 days of sick leave per year on full pay. If your absence lasts 5 consecutive days or more, we require a doctor's note (also known as a fit note) to document the absence. For shorter absences, we trust you to report your status honestly.

### Parental Leave
We support new parents fully.
*   **Primary Carer:** You are entitled to 16 weeks of parental leave on full pay.
*   **Partner Leave:** Your partner is entitled to 4 weeks of leave on full pay. This leave must be taken within the first 6 months of the child's birth or placement.

### Bereavement Leave
We offer compassionate support when you lose someone close to you.
*   **Standard:** 3 days of paid leave for the loss of a friend, relative, or close colleague.
*   **Immediate Family:** 5 days of paid leave for the loss of a partner, child, or parent.

### Jury and Public Duty Leave
If you are called for jury service or public duty (such as serving as a magistrate), you are entitled to paid leave for as long as the duty lasts. Please provide the court or official body's paperwork to People Operations so we can adjust your schedule and ensure you continue to receive your full salary during this time.

### Unpaid Leave
Sometimes, you may need extended time off that doesn't fall into the other categories. We can agree to up to 20 days of unpaid leave per year. This must be discussed and agreed upon with your manager in advance, and it will be documented in writing.

### Summary of Leave Types

| Leave Type | Entitlement | How to Request It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Annual Leave | 25 days + 8 public holidays | Submit request in shared calendar 2+ weeks in advance for >3 days |
| Sick Leave | 10 days per year (full pay) | Inform manager as soon as possible; provide note after 5 consecutive days |
| Parental Leave (Primary) | 16 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager as soon as date is known |
| Partner Leave | 4 weeks (full pay) | Notify People Operations and manager; must be taken within first 6 months |
| Bereavement Leave | 3 days (standard) / 5 days (immediate family) | Inform manager immediately; follow up with HR if extended |
| Jury/Public Duty | Full salary for duration | Provide court/official paperwork to People Operations |
| Unpaid Leave | Up to 20 days per year | Discuss and agree with manager in advance |

Who to ask: Your manager for approval and People Operations for policy questions or documentation.
