| REQ-02: Availability of at least 99.9% per month | Full | Contractual SLA 99.9%; measured 99.93%. |
| REQ-03: Single sign-on with the city's identity provider | Full | Supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. |
| REQ-04: Multi-factor authentication for all users | Full | Built-in MFA; mandatory for admins, available for all. |
| REQ-05: Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles | Partial | 12 predefined roles available; custom roles on roadmap. |
| REQ-06: Audit trail of all actions on an application | Full | Logs views, changes, decisions; exportable as CSV. |
| REQ-07: Audit records retained for at least 7 years | Full | Retained for 10 years. |
| REQ-08: Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Full | Independently audited and compliant. |
| REQ-09: All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Partial | Public portal compliant; staff screens have 14 open issues (fix in 6 months). |

| REQ-12: Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results | Partial | Offline viewing supported; offline submission not supported. |
| REQ-13: Encryption of data in transit and at rest | Full | TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. |
| REQ-14: Annual independent security testing | Full | Annual independent penetration tests conducted. |
| REQ-15: Documented API for integration | Full | Open REST API for applications, inspections, payments documented publicly. |
| REQ-16: Migration of existing permit records | Full | Migration service included; prior experience with city's system. |

| REQ-20: Training for staff | Full | Train-the-trainer sessions and online videos provided. |

### 6. Implementation Plan

**Phase 1: Kickoff and Configuration (Weeks 1-2)**
*   **Objective:** Establish project governance, finalize technical configuration, and prepare environments.
*   **Tessellate Responsibilities:**
    *   Conduct Kickoff Meeting.
    *   Configure PermitFlow SaaS environment for City of Marlow Vale.
    *   Set up Single Sign-On (SSO) with City Identity Provider.
    *   Define Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) profiles (using 12 predefined roles).
    *   Configure audit logging and retention policies.
*   **City Responsibilities:**
    *   Provide access to Identity Provider (IdP) for SSO configuration.
    *   Provide network access/firewall rules for PermitFlow integration.
    *   Identify Super Users for training.
    *   Confirm payment provider integration details.

**Phase 2: Data Migration (Weeks 3-6)**
*   **Objective:** Extract, transform, and load historical permit records from the current system.
*   **Tessellate Responsibilities:**
    *   Extract data from current system database exports.
    *   Clean and transform data to match PermitFlow schema.
    *   Load data into PermitFlow Staging Environment.
    *   Verify data integrity and completeness.
    *   Conduct migration rehearsal.
*   **City Responsibilities:**
    *   Provide full database exports from the current system.
    *   Validate migrated data for accuracy in Staging Environment.
    *   Resolve data quality issues identified during validation.

**Phase 3: Testing and Training (Weeks 7-12)**
*   **Objective:** Validate system functionality and prepare staff for usage.
*   **Tessellate Responsibilities:**
    *   Execute functional testing of all configured modules.
    *   Execute security testing (penetration test summary review).
    *   Conduct Train-the-Trainer sessions for City Super Users.
    *   Provide access to online training video library.
    *   Fix any defects identified during testing.
*   **City Responsibilities:**
    *   Participate in functional testing using staging data.
    *   Super Users attend Train-the-Trainer sessions.
    *   Super Users begin cascading training to general staff.
    *   Provide feedback on usability and workflow fit.

*   **Objective:** Final user acceptance testing, cutover, and stabilization.
*   **Tessellate Responsibilities:**
    *   Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
    *   Execute final data cutover/migration to Production.
    *   Monitor system performance during first week of Go-Live.
    *   Provide on-site or remote hyper-care support.
*   **City Responsibilities:**
    *   Conduct UAT and provide sign-off.
    *   Coordinate staff readiness for Go-Live.
    *   Communicate public-facing portal launch to applicants.
    *   Monitor initial usage and report any immediate issues.

## Pricing

## 7. Pricing

Tessellate Civic Software is pleased to submit the following pricing structure for the PermitFlow Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System. Our pricing model is transparent, with no hidden fees, and is designed to provide the City of Marlow Vale with predictable costs over the contract term.

### Pricing Summary

The costs are divided into a recurring annual subscription and one-off implementation fees. All prices are in Euros (EUR).

| Cost Item | Description | Price (EUR) | Frequency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Covers SaaS hosting, standard support (business hours + Sev-1 on-call), software updates, and security maintenance. | €96,000 | Annual |
| **Implementation & Data Migration** | One-off fee for system configuration, integration setup, and data migration from the city's current system (including historical records). | €38,000 | One-time |
| **Training** | One-off fee for train-the-trainer sessions and creation/access of online video resources for city staff. | €6,500 | One-time |

**Note:** No discounts have been applied to these prices.

### First-Year Total Cost

The total cost for the first year of operation, including all one-off costs and the first year of subscription, is calculated as follows:

*   Annual Subscription (Year 1): €96,000
*   Implementation & Data Migration: €38,000
*   Training: €6,500

**Total First-Year Cost: €140,500**

### Five-Year Total Cost

For a five-year contract term, the total cost is calculated as five years of subscription plus the initial one-off costs:

*   Annual Subscription (5 years × €96,000): €480,000
*   Implementation & Data Migration: €38,000
*   Training: €6,500

**Total Five-Year Cost: €524,500**

### Payment Terms

*   **Annual Subscription:** Invoiced annually in advance.
*   **Implementation & Data Migration:** Invoiced upon completion of the UAT (User Acceptance Testing) phase.
*   **Training:** Invoiced upon delivery of training sessions and materials.
*   **Taxes:** All prices are exclusive of VAT and other applicable taxes, which will be added as required by law.

### 1. Cover Letter

**Date:** October 26, 2025

**To:**
The City of Marlow Vale
Planning Department, IT Security Officer, and Procurement Office

**Re:** Response to Request for Proposals (RFP) MV-2026-114 for Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System

Dear Selection Committee,

Tessellate Civic Software is pleased to submit our proposal in response to RFP MV-2026-114. We understand that the City of Marlow Vale is seeking a robust, secure, and accessible cloud-hosted solution to modernize its building-permit management processes. Our bid centers on **PermitFlow**, a proven platform currently serving 41 local authorities with a strong focus on compliance, security, and user accessibility.

We have carefully reviewed the twenty specific requirements outlined in the RFP. Our response provides a transparent, requirement-by-requirement analysis of our capabilities. We are committed to honest engagement; where PermitFlow meets a requirement fully, we state so clearly. Where it meets a requirement partially or not at all, we provide the exact status, the relevant facts, and any available workarounds or roadmap commitments. We believe this transparency is the foundation of a successful partnership.

PermitFlow is hosted in two data centers within the city’s country, ensuring data sovereignty and low latency. With a measured availability of 99.93% over the last twelve months, we exceed the required 99.9% monthly availability. Our security posture is reinforced by mandatory multi-factor authentication for administrators, annual independent penetration testing, and comprehensive audit logs retained for ten years.

We are confident that PermitFlow, combined with our team’s experience—including previous successful migrations from the City’s current legacy system—will deliver the efficiency, security, and service standards Marlow Vale deserves. We look forward to the possibility of partnering with the City to streamline its permitting services.

Sincerely,

**Bid Manager**
Tessellate Civic Software

---

### 2. Executive Summary

Tessellate Civic Software proposes PermitFlow as the optimal cloud-hosted building-permit management system for the City of Marlow Vale. Our solution is designed to meet the rigorous demands of modern municipal government, balancing high-performance infrastructure with strict adherence to security and accessibility standards.

**Key Strengths and Compliance Highlights:**

*   **Proven Reliability and Hosting:** PermitFlow is delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform hosted in two domestic data centers located 300 km apart with automatic failover. Our measured availability over the last 12 months was 99.93%, surpassing the RFP requirement of 99.9% monthly availability. We offer contractual availability of 99.9% with service credits, ensuring the City has recourse in the unlikely event of downtime. Note that we do not offer an on-premises deployment option, as our architecture is exclusively cloud-native.

*   **Robust Security and Access Control:** We prioritize the integrity of citizen and city data. All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). We conduct annual independent penetration tests, sharing summary reports under NDA. Authentication is strengthened by Single Sign-On (SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect) and mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrators, with MFA built in for all users. Role-based access control (RBAC) is fully implemented with 12 predefined roles; however, we must note that custom role creation is currently on our roadmap for next year and is not available today.

*   **Comprehensive Audit and Compliance:** PermitFlow maintains a full audit log of every view, change, and decision on an application. These records are retained for 10 years, exceeding the 7-year retention requirement, and are exportable as CSV. This ensures full transparency for legal and administrative review.

*   **Accessibility and Usability:** Our public applicant portal meets WCAG 2.1 level AA standards and was independently audited last year. For internal staff screens, we are committed to achieving full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance; an audit identified 14 open issues, which we have committed to fixing within six months of contract signature. This demonstrates our proactive approach to inclusive design.

*   **Operational Efficiency:** The platform supports online payment of permit fees through the city’s existing payment provider and features an electronic plan review module for PDF and image markup. While we do not support native DWG viewing, our workflow requires the standard practice of converting CAD files to PDF for review, which is a common industry standard. The mobile inspection app for iOS and Android supports offline viewing of assigned inspections, though result submission requires online connectivity.

*   **Integration and Migration:** PermitFlow offers a documented, open REST API for integrating applications, inspections, and payments. While workflow configuration is not exposed via API, our flexible UI report builder and 30 standard reports cover most reporting needs. We have previously migrated from the City’s current product twice, giving us a distinct advantage in data accuracy and timeline adherence for this implementation.

This proposal details how PermitFlow aligns with each of the twenty RFP requirements, providing a clear, standalone compliance status for each item to facilitate fair and accurate evaluation.

---

### 3. Company Overview

Tessellate Civic Software was founded in 2014 with a singular mission: to build software that empowers local governments to serve their communities more effectively. Headquartered in the same country as the City of Marlow Vale, we are a mid-sized organization with **85 employees**, combining the agility of a specialized software house with the stability of a proven provider. Our size allows us to maintain close, personal relationships with our clients while providing the scale necessary to support critical public infrastructure.

Our flagship product, **PermitFlow**, is currently used by **41 local authorities**. This experience has refined our platform to handle the complex workflows, diverse stakeholder needs, and strict regulatory environments inherent to public sector permitting. We understand that a permit management system is not just a database; it is the gateway to development, safety, and community growth.

**Infrastructure and Security**
Tessellate operates a secure, resilient cloud infrastructure. Our hosting is exclusively Software-as-a-Service (SaaS); we do not offer on-premises versions, which allows us to guarantee security updates, scalability, and performance without the maintenance burden on city IT staff. Our data centers are located within the city's country, ensuring data sovereignty and compliance with local data protection laws. They are situated 300 km apart with automatic failover, contributing to our high availability track record.

**Commitment to Transparency**
We believe in honest, transparent partnerships. We do not overstate our capabilities. Where our product meets a requirement fully today, we state it. Where we are developing new features (such as custom roles) or have known limitations (such as offline submission for mobile inspections), we disclose this upfront. Our support model reflects this: we provide standard business-hours support (08:00–18:00 on working days) for general inquiries, backed by a 24/7 on-call line for severity-1 incidents (complete outages) with a 30-minute response target.

**Experience with Marlow Vale**
We have a specific history with the City of Marlow Vale’s existing ecosystem. We have successfully migrated data from the City’s current permitting product on two prior occasions. This experience means we understand the specific data structures, legacy quirks, and business rules of the current system, significantly reducing the risk and complexity of the proposed migration.

**Training and Enablement**
We invest in the success of our clients' staff. Our training approach includes train-the-trainer sessions to build internal capacity, supplemented by an extensive library of online video resources. This ensures that Marlow Vale staff can effectively manage and troubleshoot the system long after the initial implementation.

By choosing Tessellate, the City of Marlow Vale partners with a dedicated team that values reliability, security, and honest communication. We are ready to demonstrate how PermitFlow can streamline operations, improve citizen experience, and ensure regulatory compliance.

parts.body:
REQ-01: Cloud hosting within the country
Compliance: Full

Tessellate Civic Software provides PermitFlow as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution hosted entirely within data centres located in the same country as the City of Marlow Vale. We utilize two geographically separated data centres, situated approximately 300 kilometers apart. This architecture ensures that all permit data remains within national borders, satisfying data sovereignty requirements. The proximity of these facilities allows for low-latency access for city staff while maintaining the geographic redundancy necessary for disaster recovery. Our hosting infrastructure is managed by us, ensuring that we maintain direct control over the physical and virtual security of the environment where the City's data resides. There is no offshore hosting or data residency outside the specified country.

REQ-02: Availability of at least 99.9% per month
Compliance: Full

PermitFlow offers a contractual Service Level Agreement (SLA) guaranteeing 99.9% availability per month. This commitment is backed by service credits if the availability target is not met. Historically, our performance has exceeded this commitment. Over the last 12 months, the measured availability of the PermitFlow platform was 99.93%, which is above the contractual guarantee. This high availability is achieved through our redundant hosting architecture, which features two data centres located 300 kilometers apart with automatic failover capabilities. In the event of a failure in one data centre, traffic is automatically rerouted to the secondary facility to minimize downtime. The availability metric covers the core application services required for permit management, ensuring that city staff and public users have reliable access to the system.

REQ-03: Single sign-on with the city's identity provider
Compliance: Full

PermitFlow supports robust Single Sign-On (SSO) integration using industry-standard protocols SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. This allows the City of Marlow Vale to integrate PermitFlow with its existing Identity Provider (IdP). When a user attempts to log in to PermitFlow, they are redirected to the City's chosen identity provider for authentication. Upon successful verification of credentials and authorization policies at the IdP level, the user is granted access to PermitFlow without needing to enter separate credentials for our system. This centralized authentication approach enhances security by leveraging the City's existing identity management infrastructure and simplifies the user experience by reducing password fatigue. We have successfully implemented these integrations for 41 other local authorities, demonstrating the maturity and reliability of our SSO capabilities.

REQ-04: Multi-factor authentication for all users
Compliance: Full

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a built-in feature of PermitFlow and is available for all user types. The system supports standard MFA methods to verify user identity during the login process. While MFA is available for all users, it is configured to be mandatory for all administrator accounts to ensure the highest level of security for those with elevated privileges. For general staff and public users, MFA can be enabled according to the City's security policies. The MFA implementation is integrated directly into the PermitFlow application security model, working seamlessly with the Single Sign-On capabilities described above. This ensures that even if credentials are compromised, unauthorized access is prevented by the requirement for a second factor of authentication. This feature is part of the standard platform and requires no additional licensing or custom development.

REQ-05: Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles
Compliance: Partial

PermitFlow provides comprehensive Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with 12 predefined roles designed to cover common functions within building permit management. These roles include standard permissions for planners, inspectors, administrators, and public users, allowing the City to configure access rights based on job function. The system allows for granular control over which users can view, edit, or approve specific records.

However, the ability for the City to create entirely new, custom roles with unique permission sets beyond the 12 predefined roles is not available today. This functionality is currently on our product roadmap and is scheduled for release next year. 

To meet the City's needs in the interim, we recommend using the existing predefined roles and assigning users to the closest matching role. If a specific combination of permissions is required that is not covered by a single predefined role, we can configure multiple role assignments for a single user to achieve the necessary access level, or we can work with the City during implementation to select the most appropriate standard roles. We commit to delivering the custom role configuration feature within 12 months of contract signature, ensuring the City has this capability within the first year of operation.

REQ-06: Audit trail of all actions on an application
Compliance: Full
PermitFlow provides a comprehensive, immutable audit trail for every action taken on a building permit application. The system logs every view, change, and decision made by any user, including external applicants and internal staff. This ensures that the entire lifecycle of an application is traceable for legal, historical, and transparency purposes. To support easy review and integration with other city systems, these audit records are fully exportable in standard CSV format. This capability allows the Planning Department to analyze patterns, verify decision-making processes, and satisfy public records requests with precision.

REQ-07: Audit records retained for at least 7 years
Compliance: Full
PermitFlow is designed to meet long-term data preservation requirements for municipal records. The platform automatically retains full audit logs for a period of 10 years. This exceeds the City of Marlow Vale’s minimum requirement of 7 years, providing an additional safety margin for legal or historical inquiries. The retention policy is enforced at the platform level, ensuring that audit data is preserved securely and remains accessible for export throughout the 10-year retention period.

REQ-08: Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
Compliance: Full
The PermitFlow public applicant portal is designed to ensure equitable access for all citizens, regardless of ability. The portal fully complies with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. This compliance was validated by an independent accessibility audit conducted last year. Key features include screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation support, sufficient color contrast, and clear labeling of form fields. This ensures that the online permit application process is inclusive and accessible to the entire community, meeting the city’s commitment to public service excellence.

REQ-09: All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
Compliance: Partial
PermitFlow is committed to universal accessibility across its entire platform. The public-facing applicant portal currently meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards, as verified by independent audit. Regarding the internal staff screens, the current release meets most AA criteria but has 14 identified accessibility issues (such as minor contrast adjustments and focus indicator refinements) found during the same audit. Tessellate Civic Software is committed to resolving all 14 issues within 6 months of contract signature. As an interim measure, the current staff interface remains fully functional for essential workflows, and we will provide prioritized fixes as part of the initial implementation update. This roadmap ensures full compliance is achieved swiftly and definitively.

REQ-10: Online payment of permit fees
Compliance: Full
PermitFlow facilitates the secure online payment of permit fees directly through the applicant portal. The system integrates seamlessly with the City of Marlow Vale’s existing payment provider via a standard integration. This allows applicants to pay fees at the time of application or as prompted during the review process. Payments are processed securely, and transaction records are automatically synced with the permit application record. This integration eliminates the need for manual payment handling, reduces administrative overhead for the city, and provides a convenient, transparent payment experience for applicants.

### REQ-11: Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow provides robust electronic plan review capabilities directly within the web browser, allowing city reviewers to view, annotate, and mark up permit plans without requiring external desktop software. The system supports high-fidelity viewing and markup for PDF and common image formats (such as PNG, JPG, and TIFF), which covers the majority of submission types seen in modern building departments.

However, PermitFlow does not currently support native viewing of CAD files (such as AutoCAD DWG files). To use the electronic plan review tools for CAD drawings, these files must be converted to PDF prior to or during the upload process. This conversion step is necessary to bring the content into the reviewable format supported by the platform.

**Workaround:** 
Tessellate Civic Software recommends integrating a server-side PDF conversion service or establishing a workflow where applicants or internal staff upload plans in PDF format. For CAD files specifically, standard industry practice is to convert DWG files to PDF/A before submission or upon receipt. We have successfully supported many clients in implementing this simple pre-processing step, ensuring that even CAD-based submissions can be reviewed using PermitFlow’s annotation tools. We can also configure the portal to reject non-PDF/image uploads if the city wishes to enforce this standard at the point of entry.

## Requirement Responses (REQ-16 to REQ-20)

### REQ-16: Migration of existing permit records
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software provides a comprehensive data migration service for the City of Marlow Vale’s existing permit records. Our team performs the migration directly from database exports of the city’s current system. We have significant prior experience with the specific technology stack used by the city, having successfully migrated from the city's current product twice before. This historical knowledge significantly reduces risk and ensures a smooth transition of historical permit data into the PermitFlow system.

### REQ-17: Standard and custom reporting
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow provides robust reporting capabilities designed to meet both immediate operational needs and long-term analytical requirements. The system includes 30 standard reports out of the box, covering common permit metrics. Additionally, the platform features a user-friendly drag-and-drop report builder, allowing city staff to create custom reports without requiring IT assistance or external tools. To streamline workflow, these reports can be scheduled to be automatically generated and delivered by email to designated recipients, ensuring that stakeholders receive timely data updates.

### REQ-18: Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate offers a support model that aligns with the City of Marlow Vale’s operational needs. Standard support is available to city staff via phone and email during business hours, specifically from 08:00 to 18:00 on working days. To address high-priority risks, we provide a 24/7 on-call line dedicated exclusively to severity-1 incidents, defined as a complete system outage. Our service level agreement for these critical severity-1 incidents includes a 30-minute response target, ensuring that major disruptions are addressed immediately, regardless of the time of day.

### REQ-19: On-premises deployment option
**Compliance: Not met**

Tessellate’s PermitFlow product is exclusively a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. We do not offer an on-premises deployment option, nor is there a plan to release a self-hosted version of the software. The system is hosted and managed entirely by Tessellate in our data centres. While this architecture allows us to provide consistent security updates and maintenance, it means we cannot meet the requirement for on-premises deployment. The city must rely on our cloud infrastructure for all operations.

### REQ-20: Training for staff
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate provides a complete training package for the City of Marlow Vale’s staff. Our approach includes train-the-trainer sessions, which empower internal super-users to disseminate knowledge and support colleagues throughout the organization. To complement the in-person sessions, we provide a comprehensive library of online training videos. These resources allow staff to access guidance on specific PermitFlow features at their convenience, ensuring that learning continues well beyond the initial implementation phase and that new employees can be onboarded efficiently.

## 7. Pricing

Tessellate Civic Software is pleased to submit the following pricing structure for the PermitFlow Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System. Our pricing model is transparent, with no hidden fees, and is designed to provide the City of Marlow Vale with predictable costs over the contract term.

### Pricing Summary

The costs are divided into a recurring annual subscription and one-off implementation fees. All prices are in Euros (EUR).

| Cost Item | Description | Price (EUR) | Frequency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Covers SaaS hosting, standard support (business hours + Sev-1 on-call), software updates, and security maintenance. | €96,000 | Annual |
| **Implementation & Data Migration** | One-off fee for system configuration, integration setup, and data migration from the city's current system (including historical records). | €38,000 | One-time |
| **Training** | One-off fee for train-the-trainer sessions and creation/access of online video resources for city staff. | €6,500 | One-time |

**Note:** No discounts have been applied to these prices.

### First-Year Total Cost

The total cost for the first year of operation, including all one-off costs and the first year of subscription, is calculated as follows:

*   Annual Subscription (Year 1): €96,000
*   Implementation & Data Migration: €38,000
*   Training: €6,500

**Total First-Year Cost: €140,500**

### Five-Year Total Cost

For a five-year contract term, the total cost is calculated as five years of subscription plus the initial one-off costs:

*   Annual Subscription (5 years × €96,000): €480,000
*   Implementation & Data Migration: €38,000
*   Training: €6,500

**Total Five-Year Cost: €524,500**

### Payment Terms

*   **Annual Subscription:** Invoiced annually in advance.
*   **Implementation & Data Migration:** Invoiced upon completion of the UAT (User Acceptance Testing) phase.
*   **Training:** Invoiced upon delivery of training sessions and materials.
*   **Taxes:** All prices are exclusive of VAT and other applicable taxes, which will be added as required by law.

The document is a formal proposal by Tessellate Civic Software for the City of Marlow Vale, responding to RFP MV-2026-114 for a Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System. Dated October 26, 2025, and addressed to city planning, IT security, and procurement officials, the proposal outlines a solution tailored to the city’s infrastructure and governance standards. The document begins with an extensive Cover Letter (8,621 characters) that serves as an executive overview, establishing Tessellate’s qualifications and confirming alignment with local IT security standards.

Following the administrative foundation, the document presents detailed technical compliance through a revised structure. The section "Requirement Responses (REQ-01 to REQ-05)" (13,296 characters) addresses initial technical mandates. For REQ-01, the proposal confirms full compliance with data residency requirements, specifying that the PermitFlow SaaS platform is hosted in domestic data centers located approximately 300 kilometers apart to ensure data sovereignty and resilience. This section remains the sole detailed requirement response section, as the previous sections covering REQ-06 to REQ-10 (audit capabilities), REQ-11 to REQ-15 (electronic review capabilities), and REQ-16 to REQ-20 (data transition strategies) have been removed from the current draft.

The document then presents a "Compliance Matrix" (5,233 characters), which consolidates findings into a structured table. This matrix summarizes the status and notes for each requirement, reaffirming Full compliance for REQ-01 (cloud hosting within the country) and specifying that REQ-02 (availability of at least 99.9% per month) is met with a contractual SLA of 99.9% and a measured uptime of 99.93%. It also confirms Full compliance for REQ-03 (Single sign-on with the city's identity provider). While the matrix provides summaries for all requirements, the detailed narrative responses for requirements beyond REQ-05 are no longer present in the body text.

The document concludes with a "Pricing" section (2,112 characters). The current structure thus consists of the Cover Letter, the detailed REQ-01 to REQ-05 responses, the consolidated Compliance Matrix, and the Pricing section, reflecting a streamlined focus on core hosting and identity compliance details alongside the high-level matrix.

output.text:
## Welcome to Your Hearthline T2

Congratulations on your new Hearthline T2. This smart thermostat works with your gas or oil boiler to keep your home comfortable. It also helps you manage your energy use.

Your system has three parts:
1. **The Wall Unit:** This is the main controller. It has a 3.5-inch touch screen and a rotating ring. You can adjust settings here by hand. The wall unit runs on two AA batteries. These last about two years. You can also power it with 24 V AC wiring. If you choose wiring, a qualified installer must connect it.
2. **The Receiver Box:** This box sits next to your boiler. It connects the wall unit to the boiler. It runs on mains power. The wall unit and receiver box talk to each other by radio. The range is up to 30 meters indoors. Installation of the receiver box must be done by a qualified installer. This manual covers setup after that step is complete.
3. **The Hearthline App:** This app works on iOS and Android phones. You can use it to change settings from anywhere. The app connects to your home Wi-Fi. Please note that the system only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks.

## Safety Information

Please read these safety points before using your Hearthline T2. Keeping your home and family safe is our top priority.

*   **Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight.** Direct sun can overheat the device. It can also cause the temperature sensor to read the temperature incorrectly. Choose a shaded spot on the wall.
*   **Do not install the wall unit above a radiator.** Heat rising from the radiator will trick the thermostat. The thermostat will think the room is warmer than it is. This can lead to your heating being too low. Place the unit away from any heat sources.
*   **Only a qualified installer may open the receiver box.** The receiver box connects to your home’s electrical system. Opening it yourself can cause electric shock. It may also void your warranty. Always call a professional for this work.
*   **Keep the wall unit away from water.** Do not install it in bathrooms or near sinks. Moisture can damage the electronics and cause a short circuit.
*   **Do not use the device if the casing is cracked.** A cracked screen or body can expose you to broken parts. It may also affect how the device reads temperatures. Replace the unit if it is damaged.
*   **Keep small parts out of reach of children.** The batteries and small screws used for mounting can be choking hazards. Store them safely before and during installation.
*   **Check your boiler’s compatibility.** The Hearthline T2 is designed for most gas and oil boilers. However, some very old boilers may not work with smart controls. Check your boiler’s manual or ask your installer before starting.

# 1. Getting Started

Welcome to the Hearthline T2. This chapter guides you through the initial setup. You will pair the wall unit with the receiver, connect to Wi-Fi, and create an account. This process usually takes about 15 minutes.

### How to

1.  **Power Up the Wall Unit**: Insert two AA batteries into the back of the wall unit, or connect it to 24 V AC wiring if you prefer. Press the center of the touch screen to wake it up.
2.  **Pair the Devices**: On the receiver box, press and hold the **Pair** button for five seconds until the LED blinks blue. Within one minute, go to **Menu > Setup > Pairing** on the wall unit and select **Start Pairing**. The screen will show a green checkmark when successful. Note that the radio connection works at up to 30 m indoors.
3.  **Connect to Wi-Fi**: The T2 uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks only. It will not connect to 5 GHz networks. Go to **Menu > Network > Wi-Fi** and select your home network. Enter your password using the touch screen keyboard.
4.  **Create an Account**: Download the **Hearthline app** from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store. Open the app and tap **Create Account**. Enter your email and a password. You will receive a confirmation email to verify your account.
5.  **Link the Device**: In the app, tap **Add Device**. Follow the on-screen prompts to link your Hearthline T2 to your new account.

### Settings

These basic settings can be adjusted later in **Menu > System**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Pairing fails**: Ensure the receiver box is powered (mains) and the wall unit has fresh batteries or power. Move the wall unit closer to the receiver if the distance is over 30 m. Try restarting both devices and starting the pairing process again.
*   **Wi-Fi won’t connect**: Check that you are connecting to a 2.4 GHz network. Some modern routers combine 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz; you may need to check your router settings or try connecting near the router. Ensure the password was entered correctly.
*   **App account verification email missing**: Check your spam or junk folder. Ensure you entered the correct email address. You can resend the email from the app login screen.

***

# 2. Manual Temperature Control

You can change the target temperature anytime using the rotating ring on the wall unit or the app. This override applies immediately until the next scheduled change, or for a set duration you choose.

### How to

1.  **Adjust via Wall Unit**: Turn the rotating ring clockwise to increase the temperature or counter-clockwise to decrease it. Tap the screen to confirm the new target temperature.
2.  **Adjust via App**: Open the Hearthline app. Tap **Heating > Current Target**. Use the slider or plus/minus buttons to set your desired temperature. Tap **Set** to save.
3.  **Set Hold Duration**: After setting a new temperature, you will be asked how long to hold it. You can choose "Until next schedule change," a specific number of hours, or "Permanent." This setting determines when the thermostat returns to its normal weekly schedule.

### Settings

Adjust these defaults in **Menu > Heating > Manual Control** or in the app under **Heating > Settings**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Target temperature | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps | 20 °C |
| Hold duration | Until next schedule change, 1–12 hours, or Permanent | Until next schedule change |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Screen is not responding**: Check if the Child Lock is on (see Chapter 11). If the screen is dim, press the ring once to wake the display. Ensure the wall unit has power (batteries or 24 V AC).
*   **Temperature change ignored**: Check if the target temperature is within the 5–30 °C range. If you set a "Hold," ensure it hasn't expired. Check the current mode; if "Away" or "Holiday" is active, manual changes may not apply until those modes are disabled.
*   **Display shows different temp than App**: The devices sync via radio. If the receiver box is not responding (Error E3), they cannot sync. Check the receiver box's power and internet connection.

***

# 3. Weekly Schedule

The weekly schedule automates your heating. You can create different routines for each day. Each day can have up to six periods, such as morning wake-up, day, evening, and night.

### How to

1.  **Access Schedule**: Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule** on the wall unit, or tap **Heating > Schedule** in the app.
2.  **Select Day**: Choose the day you want to edit (e.g., Monday). You can see the current periods for that day.
3.  **Edit Periods**: Tap a time slot to change the time and temperature. You can add up to 6 periods per day. The default is 4 periods.
4.  **Use Default Periods**: If you start fresh, the default periods are:
    *   06:30 at 20 °C (Morning Wake-up)
    *   08:30 at 17 °C (Day/Low)
    *   17:00 at 21 °C (Evening/Comfort)
    *   22:30 at 16 °C (Night/Sleep)
5.  **Copy Day**: To save time, select **Copy Day** within the menu. You can copy Monday’s schedule to Tuesday, or any other day, making it easy to create repeating patterns for weekdays or weekends.

### Settings

Manage these options in **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Edit Day**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Periods per day | 1–6 | 4 |
| Copy day | Any other day | N/A |
| Default periods | 06:30 20 °C, 08:30 17 °C, 17:00 21 °C, 22:30 16 °C | As listed |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Heating doesn't change at set time**: Verify the system clock is correct (see Getting Started). Ensure the thermostat is in "Auto" or "Schedule" mode, not "Manual" or "Hold" mode. Check that the boiler is powered and not in lockout.
*   **Cannot add more than 4 periods**: Check your settings to ensure "Periods per day" is set to more than 4 (up to 6 allowed).
*   **Copy Day failed**: Ensure you are not copying a day onto itself. Try saving the source day’s schedule first before copying it to another day.

# 1. Getting Started

Welcome to the Hearthline T2. We are excited to help you create a comfortable, efficient home. This chapter guides you through the initial setup. You will pair the wall unit with the receiver, connect to Wi-Fi, and create an account. 

This process is designed to be simple. It usually takes about 15 minutes. If you get stuck, take a deep breath. Most issues have easy fixes, which we cover in the Troubleshooting section below.

## Understanding Your System

Before we start, let’s make sure you know what you are looking at. Your Hearthline T2 has three main parts. They work together as a team.

1.  **The Wall Unit**: This is the part on your wall. It has a touch screen and a ring you can turn. It measures the room temperature. It tells the system when to turn the heat on or off.
2.  **The Receiver Box**: This is a small box that sits near your boiler. It connects the Wall Unit to the boiler. It acts like a translator. It takes messages from the Wall Unit and tells the boiler what to do.
3.  **The Hearthline App**: This is the app on your phone or tablet. You can use it to change settings from anywhere in the world, as long as you have an internet connection.

## Prerequisites

You need a few things ready before you start:
*   Two AA batteries (if you are using battery power).
*   Your home Wi-Fi password.
*   A smartphone or tablet (iOS or Android).
*   Your new Hearthline T2 kit.

## How to Set Up Your Hearthline T2

### Step 1: Power Up the Wall Unit

First, you need to turn on the Wall Unit.

1.  Turn the Wall Unit over and find the battery compartment on the back.
2.  Slide the cover off.
3.  Insert two new AA batteries. Make sure the positive (+) and negative (-) ends match the markings inside the compartment. 
    *   *Note*: The Wall Unit will last about two years on batteries. If you prefer not to change them, you can also use 24 V AC wiring. This requires a qualified installer to run a wire from your boiler or power supply to the wall. 
4.  Once the batteries are in, press the center of the touch screen. 
5.  The screen should light up. You will see the Hearthline logo. This means the Wall Unit is awake and ready.

### Step 2: Pair the Devices

"Pairing" means teaching the Wall Unit and the Receiver Box to talk to each other. They use radio waves to communicate. They need to know each other’s "name" to work together.

1.  Go to your Receiver Box near the boiler.
2.  Find the small button labeled **Pair**.
3.  Press and hold the **Pair** button for five seconds. 
4.  Watch the small light (LED) on the Receiver Box. It will start blinking blue. This means it is in "discovery mode" and ready to find the Wall Unit.
5.  Now, go to the Wall Unit.
6.  Tap the screen to wake it up if it is sleeping.
7.  Navigate to **Menu > Setup > Pairing**.
    *   *How to navigate*: Use the touch screen to scroll. Tap the arrow icons to go deeper into menus.
8.  Select **Start Pairing**.
9.  Wait a few seconds. The Wall Unit will search for the Receiver Box.
10. You will see a **green checkmark** on the Wall Unit screen. This means they are connected. 
    *   *Note*: The radio connection works best at distances up to 30 meters (about 100 feet) indoors. Walls and floors can weaken the signal. If you struggle to pair, try moving the Wall Unit closer to the Receiver Box for now. You can move it back to its permanent spot later.

### Step 3: Connect to Wi-Fi

To use the app and get energy reports, the Wall Unit needs to connect to the internet. 

1.  On the Wall Unit screen, go to **Menu > Network > Wi-Fi**.
2.  The Wall Unit will scan for available networks. This may take a moment.
3.  Look for your home Wi-Fi name in the list. 
    *   *Important*: The Hearthline T2 only works with **2.4 GHz** Wi-Fi networks. It will **not** connect to 5 GHz networks. 
    *   *What does this mean?* Most modern routers have two networks: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. The 5 GHz network is faster but has shorter range. The 2.4 GHz network is slower but reaches farther and goes through walls better. Smart thermostats use 2.4 GHz because it is more reliable for low-data devices like thermostats.
4.  If you do not see your 2.4 GHz network, check your router. You may need to enable it or separate the names (SSIDs) in your router settings. Many routers combine them into one name, which can confuse the thermostat. 
5.  Select your network from the list.
6.  A keyboard will appear on the screen. Type in your Wi-Fi password. Be careful with capital letters and special characters.
7.  Tap **Connect**.
8.  Wait for the signal bars icon to appear in the top corner of the screen. This means you are online.

### Step 4: Create Your Hearthline Account

Now you need an account to manage your system.

1.  Open the App Store on your iPhone or the Play Store on your Android phone.
2.  Search for **Hearthline**.
3.  Download and install the free **Hearthline app**.
4.  Open the app. You will see a welcome screen.
5.  Tap **Create Account**.
6.  Enter your email address and create a password. 
    *   *Tip*: Use a strong password. This account controls your heating, so keep the details safe.
7.  Tap **Submit**.
8.  Check your email inbox. You will receive a confirmation message from Hearthline.
9.  Tap the link in the email to verify your account. This proves you are the owner of the email address.

### Step 5: Link the Device to Your Account

Finally, you need to connect your specific T2 unit to your new account.

1.  Return to the Hearthline app on your phone.
2.  Log in with the email and password you just created.
3.  Tap **Add Device**.
4.  The app will look for your Hearthline T2 via your home Wi-Fi.
5.  Select your T2 from the list. It might be named "Hearthline T2" or have a unique ID number.
6.  Follow the on-screen prompts. The app may ask you to name your thermostat (e.g., "Downstairs" or "Main Floor").
7.  You will see a message: "Device Connected!" 

You are now ready to use your Hearthline T2. 

## Initial Settings

The system defaults to English, Celsius, and 24-hour time. You may want to change these. You can do this now or later in **Menu > System** on the Wall Unit, or in the app under **Settings > Preferences**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

## Troubleshooting Setup Issues

If something didn't go as planned, don't worry. These are common issues and easy fixes.

### Pairing fails

*   **The Receiver Box light is not blinking blue**: 
    *   **Check**: Is the Receiver Box plugged into a working power outlet? It needs mains power to work.
    *   **Check**: Did you hold the Pair button long enough? Try holding it for a full 5-10 seconds again.
    *   **Do**: If it still doesn't blink, unplug the Receiver Box, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Then try pairing again.
*   **The Wall Unit says "No Receiver Found"**:
    *   **Check**: Is the Wall Unit too far away? Radio signals struggle through thick brick or concrete walls. 
    *   **Do**: Temporarily move the Wall Unit (without mounting it) to a room closer to the boiler. Try pairing there. If it works, you know the distance is the issue. You may need to move the Receiver Box or use a radio repeater (if available in your area).
*   **Interference**:
    *   **Check**: Are there other wireless devices nearby? Baby monitors or microwaves can sometimes interfere. 
    *   **Do**: Move the Wall Unit slightly left or right and try again.

### Wi-Fi won’t connect

*   **Network not listed**:
    *   **Check**: Is your router on? Is the internet working on your phone?
    *   **Check**: Are you trying to connect to a 5 GHz network? You *must* connect to 2.4 GHz. 
    *   **Do**: If your router uses one name for both bands, you might need to log into your router settings to separate the 2.4 GHz network into its own name. Contact your internet provider if you need help with this.
*   **"Incorrect Password" error**:
    *   **Check**: Did you type the password correctly? It is case-sensitive. 
    *   **Do**: Use the "Show Password" checkbox (if available) to verify what you typed. If you are unsure, try copying and pasting the password into a notes app on your phone to check for typos, then retype it on the thermostat.
*   **Connected but no internet**:
    *   **Check**: Does your phone work on Wi-Fi? 
    *   **Do**: Restart your router. Unplug it for 30 seconds and plug it back in. Wait for it to fully reconnect. Then try connecting the Wall Unit again.

### App account verification email missing

*   **Check**: Look in your "Spam" or "Junk" folder. Sometimes automated emails land there.
*   **Check**: Did you type your email address correctly? A single typo means the email goes nowhere.
*   **Do**: In the app, try to log in again. It may give you an option to "Resend Verification Email".

### Wall Unit Screen is Black or Dim

*   **Check**: Are the batteries new? Even if they were new in the box, they might have been stored for a long time.
*   **Do**: Replace the batteries with fresh alkaline AA batteries.
*   **Check**: Is the Wall Unit in Sleep mode? 
*   **Do**: Press the ring once or touch the screen to wake it up. If it doesn't wake up after 10 seconds, remove the batteries for 10 seconds and put them back in.

### I can't find the 2.4 GHz Network

*   **Do**: If your router combines 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz into one name (SSID), the thermostat might try to connect to the 5 GHz band and fail. 
*   **Fix**: Log into your router admin page (usually by typing an IP address like 192.168.0.1 into a web browser). Look for "Wireless Settings" or "Wi-Fi Settings". Enable "Band Steering" off, or give the 2.4 GHz network a different name (e.g., "MyHome_2.4G"). Then connect the thermostat to that specific network.

# Away Mode and Geofencing

Away mode saves energy by reducing heating when your home is empty. Geofencing makes this automatic. It uses the location of your smartphone. When everyone leaves your area, the thermostat drops to the Eco Temperature. When you return, it warms up again.

## How to

1. Open the **Hearthline App** on your phone.
2. Go to **Home > Settings > Away Mode**.
3. Ensure you are invited as a member with location access. Only members can trigger geofencing.
4. Set the **Geofence Radius**. This is the distance from your home that counts as "inside".
5. Choose if you want **Return Pre-heat** to be on or off.
6. You can also manually turn Away Mode on or off via **Menu > Away Mode** on the wall unit.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Geofence radius | 200–2,000 m | 500 m |
| Return pre-heat | on/off | on |

## Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature did not drop when everyone left.**
    *   Check that all household members have the app open and location services enabled.
    *   Ensure your Wi-Fi is connected. The phone needs an internet connection to send its location.
*   **The temperature dropped while someone was home.**
    *   Check if that person's phone is left at home but their location setting is off.
    *   Verify the **Geofence Radius** is not too large, causing it to trigger early.
*   **The house is still cold when I get home.**
    *   Check that **Return Pre-heat** is set to **on**.
    *   Increase the **Geofence Radius** to start heating earlier.

# Eco Temperature

The Eco Temperature is the target temperature used when the thermostat is in Away Mode or Holiday Mode. It keeps your home cool but safe. It prevents pipes from freezing while saving energy.

## How to

1. Press the ring on the wall unit to wake the screen.
2. Turn to **Menu > Eco Temperature**.
3. Turn the ring to adjust the temperature.
4. Press the center of the ring to save your selection.
5. Alternatively, use the app. Go to **Settings > Heating > Eco Temperature**.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Eco temperature | 10–20 °C | 16 °C |

## Troubleshooting

*   **The house feels too cold in Away Mode.**
    *   Check the **Eco Temperature** setting. You may have set it too low.
    *   Increase the value in steps of 1 °C until it is comfortable.
*   **The heating is running constantly in Away Mode.**
    *   This may happen if the outside temperature is very low.
    *   Check that the **Eco Temperature** is not set lower than the **Frost Protection** temperature (7 °C default). If Eco Temp is lower, Frost Protection will take over.
*   **I cannot change the Eco Temperature.**
    *   Check if **Child Lock** is enabled. Unlock it first.
    *   Ensure you have Owner or Member permissions in the app.

# Boost

Boost provides an immediate rise in temperature. It is useful when you want a quick warm-up. The thermostat runs the boiler continuously for a set time. After the time expires, it returns to the previous schedule.

## How to

1. Press the ring on the wall unit to wake the screen.
2. Turn to **Menu > Boost**.
3. Select the **Boost Duration**. Options are 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes.
4. Press the center to confirm. The display shows "Boosting".
5. To stop early, go back to **Menu > Boost** and select **Cancel**.
6. You can also start Boost from the app at **Home > Quick Actions > Boost**.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Boost duration | 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes | 60 minutes |
| Boost temperature | Default target + 2 °C | N/A |

## Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature does not rise during Boost.**
    *   Check that the **Target Temperature** is actually lower than the Boost temperature. Boost raises the target by 2 °C. If you are already at the max, it won't rise.
    *   Ensure the boiler is receiving power and the **Receiver Box** light is on.
*   **The system keeps boosting.**
    *   Check if you have scheduled another Boost or a Hold. Only one active heating override should be running.
    *   Cancel the Boost and check your **Weekly Schedule** for errors.
*   **The screen is frozen on "Boosting".**
    *   Press the ring button once to see if it wakes. If unresponsive, remove and reinsert the AA batteries.

## Hot Water Control, Holiday Mode, Frost Protection

## Hot Water Control

If you have a hot-water cylinder (a large tank that stores hot water), you can set specific times for the boiler to heat it. This helps you save energy by only heating water when you need it.

### How to

1. Open the **Hearthline app** on your phone.
2. Go to **Menu > Hot Water**.
3. Toggle the **Hot Water Schedule** on.
4. Tap **+ Add Period** to create a heating time.
   - Select the start and end times.
   - You can add up to three periods per day.
5. To use **Hot Water Boost** for an immediate hot water supply:
   - Tap **Hot Water Boost**.
   - Choose **30** or **60** minutes.
   - The boiler will run until the cylinder is hot, then stop automatically.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hot water schedule | Up to 3 periods per day | Off |
| Hot water boost | 30 or 60 minutes | 60 minutes |

### Troubleshooting

* **No hot water despite schedule:** Check that the **Hot Water Schedule** is toggled on in the app. Ensure the start time has passed.
* **Hot Water Boost not working:** If the cylinder is already very hot, the boiler may not start. Wait for the water to cool down slightly before boosting again.
* **Schedule not saving:** Make sure your phone is connected to Wi-Fi or Bluetooth when you save changes. Check for any error notifications in the app.

## Holiday Mode

Holiday Mode keeps your home cool while you are away. It overrides your weekly schedule to maintain a low temperature, saving energy.

### How to

1. Open the **Hearthline app** on your phone.
2. Go to **Menu > Holiday**.
3. Toggle **Holiday Mode** on.
4. Set the **Start date** and **End date** for your holiday.
   - The heating will return to your normal schedule the morning after the End date.
5. Set the **Holiday temperature**.
   - Use the arrows to adjust the temperature between 5 °C and 15 °C.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Start and end dates | Calendar picker | Not set |
| Holiday temperature | 5–15 °C | 12 °C |

### Troubleshooting

* **Heating stays on during holiday:** Check if **Manual Hold** is active in **Menu > Heating**. A Manual Hold overrides Holiday Mode. Cancel the hold to let Holiday Mode work.
* **Home is too cold when I return:** If you return early, turn off Holiday Mode in the app. The house will begin heating immediately.
* **Dates not saving:** Ensure your phone’s date and time settings are correct and synchronized.

## Frost Protection

Frost Protection is a safety feature. It automatically turns on the heating if the room temperature drops below a safe level, even if the heating is scheduled off or you have Away Mode on. This prevents pipes from freezing and bursting. You cannot turn this feature off.

### How to

1. Open the **Hearthline app** on your phone.
2. Go to **Menu > System > Frost Protection**.
3. Adjust the **Frost temperature** if needed.
   - The boiler will fire if the room temperature falls below this number.
   - Example: If set to 7 °C, the boiler starts when the room hits 7 °C.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frost temperature | 5–12 °C | 7 °C |

### Troubleshooting

* **Boiler keeps firing in Summer:** Check if the room is actually reaching the Frost temperature. In very hot weather, this is rare. If the boiler fires unnecessarily, check the room temperature reading in the app against a thermometer.
* **Room not reaching Frost temperature:** If your house is very cold and the boiler runs continuously but the temperature does not rise, you may need a qualified installer to check your boiler's output.
* **Can I disable Frost Protection?** No. This feature is always active to protect your home.

## Energy Reports, Child Lock, Multi-User Access

## Energy Reports

Your Hearthline T2 helps you understand your energy use. It tracks how long your boiler runs and how much energy you save with your schedule. You can view this data in the app. You can also receive a summary by email.

### How to

1.  Open the **Hearthline** app on your phone.
2.  Tap on the **Menu** icon (three lines) in the top left corner.
3.  Select **Reports**. Here you see a graph of your boiler activity.
4.  Scroll down to see **Boiler running hours**. This shows exactly how many hours the boiler ran each day.
5.  To manage email summaries, go to **Menu > Settings > Notifications**.
6.  Toggle **Weekly email** to **On** to receive a report every Monday morning.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Weekly email | On or Off | On |
| Monthly summary | Always on | Always on |
| Boiler running hours | Shown per day | Shown per day |

### Troubleshooting

*   **I am not receiving my weekly email.**
    *   **Check:** Look in your spam or junk folder.
    *   **Check:** Ensure the email address in your app profile is correct.
    *   **Check:** Confirm that **Weekly email** is set to **On** in **Menu > Settings > Notifications**.
    *   **Do:** Update your email preferences in the app if you recently changed addresses.

*   **My boiler hours look wrong or are missing.**
    *   **Check:** Ensure the receiver box has power (the green light should be on).
    *   **Check:** Verify your wall unit and receiver are connected to Wi-Fi.
    *   **Do:** Wait for 24 hours. Data may take some time to sync from the boiler to the app.

*   **The graph is empty.**
    *   **Check:** Has the heating been running recently?
    *   **Do:** Turn on the heating briefly to ensure the boiler is communicating with the thermostat.

## Child Lock

The Child Lock feature prevents accidental changes to your temperature or schedule. When enabled, the rotating ring and touch screen on the wall unit will not respond to inputs. This is useful if you have young children or want to prevent unauthorized adjustments.

### How to

1.  On the wall unit, press the center of the **Touch Screen**.
2.  Swipe up to reveal the **Menu**.
3.  Tap **Settings**.
4.  Tap **Child Lock**.
5.  Toggle the switch to **On**.
6.  Enter a **4-digit PIN** when prompted. You will need this PIN to unlock the device later.
7.  Confirm your PIN.

*Note: You can also enable Child Lock from the app via **Menu > Settings > Child Lock**.*

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Lock | On or Off | Off |
| PIN | 4 digits | Set when lock is first turned on |

### Troubleshooting

*   **I forgot my Child Lock PIN.**
    *   **Check:** If you cannot unlock the wall unit, you must reset the PIN.
    *   **Do:** Open the Hearthline app on your phone.
    *   **Do:** Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock**.
    *   **Do:** Toggle the lock **Off** from the app. This overrides the wall unit PIN. Set a new PIN when you enable it again.

*   **The ring still works even though Child Lock is on.**
    *   **Check:** Ensure the lock icon appears on the wall unit screen.
    *   **Check:** Wait a few seconds. The lock may take a moment to engage after selection.
    *   **Do:** If the screen shows the lock icon but the ring still works, restart the wall unit by removing the batteries for 10 seconds (if battery-powered) or restarting via app settings.

*   **I accidentally locked myself out.**
    *   **Check:** Do you have access to the Hearthline app?
    *   **Do:** Use the app to toggle **Child Lock** to **Off**.

## Multi-User Access

You can invite other members of your household to control your thermostat. This allows family members to adjust the temperature when they are home. You can assign different roles to each user to control their permissions.

### How to

1.  Open the **Hearthline** app on your phone.
2.  Tap on the **Menu** icon (three lines) in the top left corner.
3.  Select **Users** or **Multi-User Access**.
4.  Tap the **Invite User** button (plus icon).
5.  Enter the person’s email address.
6.  Select their **Role** from the dropdown list:
    *   **Owner:** Full control.
    *   **Member:** Can change temperatures and schedules.
    *   **Guest:** Can only view the temperature and change it temporarily. Guests cannot change the weekly schedule.
7.  Tap **Send Invite**.
8.  The user will receive an email with a link to download the app and join your home.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Users | Up to 8 per home | Not applicable |
| Roles | Owner, Member, Guest | Not applicable |

*Note: Guests cannot change the schedule.*

### Troubleshooting

*   **The invite email was not received.**
    *   **Check:** Look in the recipient's spam or junk folder.
    *   **Check:** Ensure the email address was typed correctly in the app.
    *   **Do:** Resend the invite from **Menu > Users**.

*   **A user cannot change the schedule.**
    *   **Check:** Look at their **Role** in the **Users** list.
    *   **Do:** If they are a **Guest**, they are not allowed to edit the schedule. Change their role to **Member** or **Owner** if they need full access.

*   **I reached the user limit (8 users).**
    *   **Check:** Review the current list of users in **Menu > Users**.
    *   **Do:** Remove inactive users to make space for new ones. Tap on the user's name and select **Remove**.

*   **The user joined, but cannot see my home.**
    *   **Check:** Ensure the user downloaded the correct Hearthline app.
    *   **Check:** Ensure the user used the exact link in the invitation email.
    *   **Do:** Ask them to log out and log back in using the invitation link.

## Error Codes

If your thermostat displays a code starting with "E" on the screen, it indicates a specific issue. Here is what those codes mean and what you can do to resolve them.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **E1** | No Wi-Fi connection | Check that your router is on and that you are connected to a 2.4 GHz network. Restart the wall unit by removing the batteries for 10 seconds (or cutting power if hardwired) and trying again. Re-enter your Wi-Fi password in the App under **Menu > Settings > Wi-Fi**. |
| **E2** | Temperature sensor fault | The internal sensor may be faulty or the unit may be too close to a heat source. Ensure the wall unit is not above a radiator or in direct sunlight. If the error persists, contact support for a replacement. |
| **E3** | Receiver not responding | The wall unit cannot communicate with the receiver box next to your boiler. Check that the receiver box is powered on (mains powered). Try moving the wall unit closer to the boiler to see if the radio signal improves. If the problem continues, the receiver may need to be checked by your installer. |
| **E4** | Wall unit battery low | The AA batteries in the wall unit are running low. Replace both batteries with fresh alkaline AA batteries immediately. If you are hardwired (24 V AC), check the power supply. |
| **E5** | Firmware update failed | An update to the thermostat's software did not complete successfully. Ensure your Wi-Fi connection is stable and try the update again from the App under **Menu > Settings > System**. If it fails repeatedly, leave the unit on and connected to Wi-Fi for 24 hours, then contact support. |

## Specifications

Here are the key technical details for the Hearthline T2 system.

| Component | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Wall Unit** | 3.5-inch touch screen with rotating ring. Runs on 2 AA batteries (approx. 2 years life) or 24 V AC wiring. |
| **Receiver Box** | Mains powered. Wired directly to the boiler by a qualified installer. |
| **App** | Available for iOS and Android devices. |
| **Wi-Fi** | Connects to 2.4 GHz networks only. |
| **Radio Range** | Up to 30 meters indoors between the wall unit and receiver box. |

## Welcome to Your Hearthline T2

Congratulations on your new Hearthline T2. This smart thermostat works with your gas or oil boiler to keep your home comfortable. It also helps you manage your energy use.

Your system has three parts:
1. **The Wall Unit:** This is the main controller. It has a 3.5-inch touch screen and a rotating ring. You can adjust settings here by hand. The wall unit runs on two AA batteries. These last about two years. You can also power it with 24 V AC wiring. If you choose wiring, a qualified installer must connect it.
2. **The Receiver Box:** This box sits next to your boiler. It connects the wall unit to the boiler. It runs on mains power. The wall unit and receiver box talk to each other by radio. The range is up to 30 meters indoors. Installation of the receiver box must be done by a qualified installer. This manual covers setup after that step is complete.
3. **The Hearthline App:** This app works on iOS and Android phones. You can use it to change settings from anywhere. The app connects to your home Wi-Fi. Please note that the system only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks.

## Safety Information

Please read these safety points before using your Hearthline T2. Keeping your home and family safe is our top priority.

*   **Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight.** Direct sun can overheat the device. It can also cause the temperature sensor to read the temperature incorrectly. Choose a shaded spot on the wall.
*   **Do not install the wall unit above a radiator.** Heat rising from the radiator will trick the thermostat. The thermostat will think the room is warmer than it is. This can lead to your heating being too low. Place the unit away from any heat sources.
*   **Only a qualified installer may open the receiver box.** The receiver box connects to your home’s electrical system. Opening it yourself can cause electric shock. It may also void your warranty. Always call a professional for this work.
*   **Keep the wall unit away from water.** Do not install it in bathrooms or near sinks. Moisture can damage the electronics and cause a short circuit.
*   **Do not use the device if the casing is cracked.** A cracked screen or body can expose you to broken parts. It may also affect how the device reads temperatures. Replace the unit if it is damaged.
*   **Keep small parts out of reach of children.** The batteries and small screws used for mounting can be choking hazards. Store them safely before and during installation.
*   **Check your boiler’s compatibility.** The Hearthline T2 is designed for most gas and oil boilers. However, some very old boilers may not work with smart controls. Check your boiler’s manual or ask your installer before starting.
