parts.body:
# Product Requirements Document: Inkwell

## 1. Overview

Inkwell is a fast, private, offline-first note-taking application designed for web, iOS, and Android platforms. The core value proposition rests on three pillars: speed, privacy, and seamless synchronicity. Unlike cloud-centric competitors that require constant connectivity, Inkwell treats local data as the source of truth, syncing changes only when connectivity is available. This architecture ensures that users can capture and retrieve information instantly, regardless of their network status.

**Product Summary**
Inkwell allows users to create rich-text notes with Markdown shortcuts, organize them into hierarchical notebooks and flat tags, and sync across devices. The application supports attachments, including images and PDFs, with future support for web clipping and PDF annotation. 

**Target Audience**
The primary users are knowledge workers who value privacy and speed: students capturing lectures, consultants documenting meetings, and researchers managing large volumes of unstructured data. 

**Business Model**
The application follows a freemium model:
- **Free Tier**: Up to 3 devices, 500 MB attachment storage, no version history.
- **Inkwell Plus (€4/month)**: Unlimited devices, 10 GB attachment storage, 30 days of version history, and priority support.

**Technical Context**
The application must be offline-first. All CRUD operations happen locally against a persistent local store (SQLite/Realm/IndexedDB depending on platform). Background jobs handle bi-directional sync with the cloud backend when connectivity is restored. Conflict resolution strategies must be defined and tested rigorously.

## 2. Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals

1.  **Instant Interaction**: The UI must remain responsive (<16ms frame time) even when interacting with large datasets (10,000+ notes). Opening a single note (<1 MB) must happen in <300ms (p95) on mid-range mobile devices.
2.  **True Offline Capability**: Users must be able to create, edit, delete, search, and organize notes without any internet connection. Sync must be transparent and eventual.
3.  **Cross-Platform Consistency**: The core feature set (create, edit, organize, sync) must work identically on iOS, Android, and Web. The native feel is crucial; we are not building a wrapped web app for mobile.
4.  **Privacy by Design**: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) is not required for v1, but data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). We must demonstrate compliance with GDPR/CCPA standards.
5.  **Fast Search**: Full-text search across 10,000 notes must return results in <500ms (p95) offline.

### Non-Goals

1.  **Collaborative Real-Time Editing**: We will not support simultaneous editing by multiple users on the same note in v1. This increases complexity significantly (CRDTs/OT) and is not a core persona need.
2.  **Advanced Database Features**: We will not implement relational databases, formulas, or backlinks (Obsidian-style) in v1. The focus is on linear text and hierarchical organization.
3.  **Web Clipper for All Browsers**: In v1, we will support a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox only. Safari is deferred to post-MVP.
4.  **Video/Audio Recording**: Direct recording of audio/video into the editor is out of scope. Users can attach existing files, but recording logic is too complex for the first release.
5.  **Native Widget Customization**: While widgets are needed for quick capture, deep customization options (changing colors, data points displayed) are post-MVP.

## 3. Personas

The product decisions and feature prioritization are driven by three primary personas derived from user research.

### Persona 1: Maya (The Student)
- **Demographics**: 21 years old, University Student, uses a MacBook and an iPhone.
- **Behaviors**: Takes notes during fast-paced lectures. Switches devices frequently (laptop to phone on the commute). Often works in areas with poor connectivity (basement lecture halls, subway).
- **Goals**: Capture information quickly using keyboard shortcuts. Review notes on the go. Find specific keywords from months ago.
- **Pain Points**: Cloud-only apps freeze when wifi drops. Losing notes during sync conflicts. Cluttered interfaces that slow down typing.
- **Inkwell Fit**: Offline-first ensures she never loses a note during a lecture. Sync handles the laptop-to-phone transition seamlessly. Fast search helps her study.

### Persona 2: Daniel (The Consultant)
- **Demographics**: 34 years old, Management Consultant, uses an iPad Pro and an Android phone.
- **Behaviors**: Creates 10-20 notes per day from meetings. Needs to recall client-specific details from years ago. High volume of text-based content.
- **Goals**: Organize notes by client/project (notebooks). Find information across a growing archive (10k+ notes). Share notes via export (PDF/Markdown) for client deliverables.
- **Pain Points**: Finding a specific meeting note from two years ago takes too long. Exporting notes breaks formatting. Privacy concerns with client data in the cloud.
- **Inkwell Fit**: Robust tagging/notebooks for organization. Fast, indexed search across large datasets. Secure storage (AES-256) reassures privacy concerns. Export features enable client sharing.

### Persona 3: Aiko (The Researcher)
- **Demographics**: 29 years old, Academic Researcher, uses a Windows Desktop and an Android tablet.
- **Behaviors**: Reads many PDFs and web articles. Clips content from the web. Annotates PDFs directly. Needs to cross-reference sources.
- **Goals**: Keep original source material (PDFs/Web clips) alongside notes. Organize by topic. Preserve formatting from the web.
- **Pain Points**: Copy-pasting from the web loses formatting. Finding the source of a pasted paragraph is impossible. Large PDFs slow down note apps.
- **Inkwell Fit**: PDF attachment and annotation support (post-MVP, but core to roadmap). Web clipping. Robust tagging to cross-reference sources. 

## 4. User Stories

The following user stories define the functional requirements for the MVP. Each story includes acceptance criteria in the Given/When/Then format for testability.

### US-01: Create a note
**Story**: As a Maya, I want to quickly create a new note, so that I can start typing my lecture content immediately.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am on the main notes screen, when I tap the "New Note" button, then a new blank note editor should open within 300ms.
- Given I am in a new note, when I type text, then the title should automatically be derived from the first line if no title is explicitly set.
- Given I have created a note with content, when I navigate back to the notes list, then the note should appear in the list immediately with its auto-generated title and preview text.

### US-02: Edit with Markdown shortcuts
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to use Markdown shortcuts while typing, so that I can format my meeting minutes efficiently without reaching for the mouse.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am in the note editor, when I type `# ` at the start of a line, then the line should transform into a Heading 1.
- Given I am in the note editor, when I type `* ` or `- ` at the start of a line, then the line should transform into a bullet list.
- Given I am in the note editor, when I select text and press `Ctrl+B` (or Cmd+B on Mac/iOS), then the selected text should be bolded.
- Given I am in the note editor, when I type `> ` at the start of a line, then the line should transform into a blockquote.

### US-03: Organise notes in notebooks
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to organize my notes into notebooks, so that I can separate notes by client or project.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am on the sidebar or menu, when I select "Create Notebook" and enter a name, then a new notebook should be created and appear in the notebook list.
- Given I have a note selected, when I drag and drop it onto a notebook in the sidebar, then the note should be assigned to that notebook and the UI should confirm the move.
- Given I am viewing a specific notebook, when I open the notebook, then only notes assigned to that notebook (and its sub-notebooks, if nested) should be displayed.

### US-04: Tag notes
**Story**: As a Maya, I want to tag my notes, so that I can group related lectures by topic across different notebooks.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am editing a note, when I type `#tag` in the body, then the tag should be highlighted and added to the note's metadata.
- Given I am viewing a note, when I tap the "Add Tag" button and type a tag name, then the tag should be applied to the note.
- Given I have tagged multiple notes with "#physics", when I click the tag in the sidebar or search results, then only notes containing that tag should be displayed.

### US-05: Full-text search
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to search for text across all my notes, so that I can find specific details from past meetings quickly.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I have 10,000 notes, when I type a search query in the global search bar, then results should start appearing in under 500ms (p95).
- Given I type a search query, when the results appear, then the matching text within the note previews should be highlighted.
- Given I am offline, when I perform a search, then the results should still appear locally (offline-first search index).
- Given I search for a word that doesn't exist, when I press enter, then a "No results found" message should be displayed.

### US-06: Work offline
**Story**: As a Maya, I want to use the app without an internet connection, so that I can take notes in lecture halls with poor Wi-Fi.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am in airplane mode, when I create a new note, then the note should be saved to the local database and be accessible in the notes list.
- Given I am offline, when I edit an existing note, then the changes should be saved locally and reflected in the UI immediately.
- Given I am offline, when I delete a note, then it should be removed from the local view immediately.
- Given I am offline, when I attempt to sync, then the app should indicate that sync is pending until connectivity is restored, without throwing a hard error.

### US-07: Sync across devices
**Story**: As a Maya, I want my notes to sync across my laptop and phone, so that I can review notes taken on my laptop on my phone during the commute.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I create a note on Device A, when I switch to Device B (connected to the same account), then the new note should appear on Device B within 10 seconds of Device A connecting to the internet.
- Given I edit a note on Device A, when I open the note on Device B, then the latest version from Device A should be displayed (last-write-wins or conflict resolution logic applied).
- Given I am on Device A and Device B, and I edit the same note simultaneously while both are offline, when they reconnect, then a conflict resolution mechanism should preserve both changes (e.g., create a conflicting copy or merge).

### US-08: Attach images and PDFs
**Story**: As a Maya, I want to attach images and PDFs to my notes, so that I can include slides and diagrams from lectures.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am editing a note, when I click the "Attach" button and select an image file (JPG/PNG), then the image should be embedded in the note and uploaded to storage.
- Given I am editing a note, when I drag and drop a PDF file into the editor, then a link/preview card for the PDF should be inserted.
- Given I have an image attached, when I click on it, then it should open in a full-screen viewer.

### US-09: Clip a web page
**Story**: As a Aiko, I want to clip web pages, so that I can save articles for research without copying and pasting.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am in the browser extension, when I click the "Clip" button, then the current page content (title, text, and primary images) should be captured and saved as a new note in Inkwell.
- Given I clip a page, when the note is created, then the source URL should be preserved in the note metadata or header.
- Given I clip a page, when the sync completes, then the clipped note should be available on all my devices.

### US-10: Annotate a PDF
**Story**: As a Aiko, I want to annotate PDFs, so that I can highlight and comment on research papers directly.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I have a PDF attached to a note, when I tap/click the PDF to open it in the viewer, then I should see annotation tools (highlight, pen, text).
- Given I use the highlight tool on text in a PDF, when I release the touch/mouse, then the highlight should be visible in the viewer.
- Given I have added annotations to a PDF, when I close the viewer, then the annotations should be saved and persisted with the PDF attachment.

### US-11: Pin and favourite notes
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to pin important notes to the top of my list, so that I can access active project notes quickly.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am viewing a note, when I tap the "Pin" icon, then the note should move to the top of the notes list and display a pin icon.
- Given I have pinned notes, when I open the app, then pinned notes should remain at the top of the list regardless of modification date.
- Given I tap the "Pin" icon on a pinned note, then the pin should be removed and the note should return to its chronological position.

### US-12: Trash and restore
**Story**: As a Maya, I want to recover accidentally deleted notes, so that I don't lose important lecture content.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I delete a note, when I navigate to the "Trash" section, then the note should appear in the trash list.
- Given I have a note in the Trash, when I select it and click "Restore", then the note should return to its original notebook.
- Given a note is in the Trash, when 30 days have passed, then the note should be permanently deleted from the server and all devices.

### US-13: Export notes
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to export my notes, so that I can share formatted meeting minutes with clients.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am viewing a note, when I select "Export" and choose "PDF", then a PDF file containing the note's content and formatting should be downloaded/shared.
- Given I am viewing a note, when I select "Export" and choose "Markdown", then a `.md` file containing the raw Markdown text should be downloaded/shared.
- Given I export a note with images, when I choose "PDF", then the images should be embedded in the resulting PDF.

### US-14: Version history
**Story**: As a Daniel, I want to view version history, so that I can revert to a previous state of a meeting note if I made an error.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I have edited a note, when I open the "Version History" menu, then a list of previous versions with timestamps should be displayed.
- Given I select a previous version, when I click "Preview", then the content of that version should be displayed.
- Given I select a previous version, when I click "Restore", then the current note should be overwritten with the content from that version.
- Given I am on the Free plan, when I try to access Version History, then the feature should be locked with an upsell prompt.

### US-15: Lock a note
**Story**: As a Aiko, I want to lock sensitive notes with a PIN, so that my private research data is secure if my device is shared.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given I am viewing a note, when I tap "Lock Note", then the note should require a PIN or biometric authentication to open.
- Given a note is locked, when I try to open it, then a PIN entry screen or biometric prompt should appear.
- Given I enter the correct PIN, when the authentication succeeds, then the note content should be displayed.

**NFR-9: Resource Usage**

2.  **Perceived "Incomplete" Product**: Many competitors (Evernote, OneNote) support images out of the box. Users like Maya may expect to paste screenshots of lecture slides immediately. The absence of US-08 may lead to high initial churn if the "rich text" promise isn't fully met.
3.  **Sync Complexity in v1.1**: Introducing attachments later means retrofitting the sync engine to handle binary blobs efficiently. This is a high-risk technical debt payoff that could destabilize the stable text-only sync we launch with.
4.  **Monetization Delay**: Attachments are a key differentiator for the Plus tier. Delaying US-08 reduces the immediate perceived value of the upgrade path, potentially slowing down the **Paid Conversion** metric in the first 6 months.

## 8. Open Questions

*   **Conflict Resolution Granularity**: Should we use block-level diffs or full-note snapshots for conflict resolution? Block-level is better for UX but significantly more complex to implement and debug. Current assumption: Full-note snapshots with user choice, but this needs final engineering sign-off.
*   **Search Index Storage Budget**: What is the maximum allowable disk space for the local search index on low-storage devices (e.g., 64GB iPhone SE)? If a user exceeds this, do we degrade search performance or disable full-text search for older notes?
*   **Clock Skew Handling**: How should the sync engine handle devices with significant clock drift (>5 minutes) to ensure correct "last-write-wins" logic? We need to decide if we rely solely on device time or incorporate a logical clock (Lamport timestamp) in v1.
*   **Offline Sync Queue Overflow**: If a user makes 500+ edits while offline for several days, what is the maximum size/depth of the local sync queue before we force a partial sync or warn the user? We need to prevent app crashes from memory exhaustion.
*   **Markdown Compatibility Scope**: Do we strictly support CommonMark, or do we extend to support GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) for tables and task lists? Aiko and Daniel have requested table support, but tables are complex to edit with keyboard shortcuts on mobile.
*   **Beta Migration Path**: If we release a beta before the final schema is locked, how do we handle breaking changes for beta testers? Do we wipe local data, or do we build a migration tool?
*   **Export Formatting Fidelity**: How much fidelity is required for PDF export? We need to decide if we must support custom fonts and complex nested lists, or if a "clean, standard document" approach is acceptable for MVP. Complex formatting often breaks PDF engines.
*   **Account Deletion Propagation**: What is the exact user-visible state when a user deletes their account while one of their devices is offline? Should the device continue to function until reconnected, or should it lock itself immediately? Legal requires deletion, but UX requires non-disruptiveness.
*   **Widget Data Scope**: For the quick-capture widget on iOS/Android, how much data can we preload before causing widget load timeouts? We need to define the max number of recent notes displayed in the widget.

## 5. Non-Functional Requirements

These requirements define the technical constraints and quality standards that must be met for the MVP release. They are binding for engineering planning and QA acceptance.

**NFR-1: Note Load Performance**
The application must open a standard text note (size < 1 MB) in under 300 milliseconds (p95) on mid-range mobile devices (e.g., iPhone SE, Pixel 6a). This ensures the "instant capture" promise for personas like Maya during fast-paced lectures.

**NFR-2: Search Performance**
Full-text search across a local database of 10,000 notes must return the first set of results in under 500 milliseconds (p95), while the device is completely offline. This is critical for Daniel, who relies on finding old client notes quickly.

**NFR-3: Sync Latency**
Edits made while offline must sync to the server and propagate to other logged-in devices within 10 seconds of the source device regaining internet connectivity. The UI must provide visual feedback (e.g., a subtle spinner or icon change) during this process.

**NFR-4: Sync Service Availability**
The sync backend service must maintain a monthly availability of 99.9% or higher, measured as the percentage of time the API endpoints are responsive and returning successful status codes.

**NFR-5: Data Encryption**
All user data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 on both the device (local database) and the server. All data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher. This meets the privacy expectations of Daniel and Aiko regarding client/research data.

**NFR-6: Accessibility**
The application must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards across all platforms. This includes support for VoiceOver/TalkBack, sufficient color contrast ratios, and keyboard navigation for the note editor on desktop/web.

**NFR-7: Platform Support**

**NFR-8: Offline Resilience**

**NFR-9: Resource Usage**

## 6. Success Metrics

The following metrics will be tracked to evaluate the success of the launch and the health of the product over the first six months.

| Metric | Definition | Target at 6 months after launch |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Activation Rate** | Percentage of new signups who create at least one note within 24 hours of registration. | 40% |
| **D30 Retention** | Percentage of users from a given signup cohort who open the app on Day 30 post-signup. | 15% |
| **Sync Success Rate** | Percentage of sync operations that complete without error within the 10-second target window. | 95% |
| **Search Latency (P95)** | The 95th percentile of time taken to return search results for a query in an offline index of 10,000+ notes. | < 500 ms |
| **Paid Conversion** | Percentage of active free users who upgrade to the Inkwell Plus plan. | 2.0% |

## 7. MVP Cut

To meet the release date with a 14-person team, the MVP scope is strictly limited to the core "capture, organize, retrieve, sync" loop. We prioritize data integrity and speed over media handling and advanced collaboration features.

### In the MVP

The following eight user stories are included in the initial release:

*   **US-01: Create a note** (Mandatory: Core functionality)
*   **US-02: Edit with Markdown shortcuts** (Mandatory: Core editing experience)
*   **US-05: Full-text search** (Mandatory: Core value for Daniel)
*   **US-06: Work offline** (Mandatory: Core architectural guarantee)
*   **US-07: Sync across devices** (Mandatory: Core value for Maya)
*   **US-03: Organise notes in notebooks** (Chosen: Critical for Daniel’s client-based organization and Maya’s course separation. Without this, the app is an unusable flat list for power users.)
*   **US-04: Tag notes** (Chosen: Complements notebooks for cross-cutting organization, essential for Aiko’s and Daniel’s cross-referencing needs.)
*   **US-12: Trash and restore** (Chosen: Essential for user trust. Accidental deletion is the highest risk to user retention for a note-taking app. Implementing a robust trash system is lower complexity than attachment syncing and prevents catastrophic data loss complaints.)

### After the MVP

The following stories are deferred to post-MVP releases (v1.1+):

*   **US-08: Attach images and PDFs** (Deferred due to high complexity in binary sync, storage limits enforcement, and UI rendering across platforms. Attachments are a significant source of sync conflicts and storage costs.)
*   **US-09: Clip a web page** (Deferred as it requires a browser extension and content extraction heuristics, which are distinct from the core app.)
*   **US-10: Annotate a PDF** (Deferred as it depends on US-08 and requires a complex PDF rendering/annotation engine.)
*   **US-11: Pin and favourite notes** (Deferred as a nice-to-have UX improvement; users can use a notebook named "Pinned" as a workaround.)
*   **US-13: Export notes** (Deferred as PDF generation engines are heavy and buggy; initial focus is on internal note-taking. Markdown export is simple but bundled with PDF for v1.1.)
*   **US-14: Version history** (Deferred as Plus feature; requires significant storage overhead and UI for diffs.)
*   **US-15: Lock a note** (Deferred as it adds security implementation complexity; app-level lock is sufficient for MVP.)

### Risks of the Cut

1.  **Persona Mismatch for Aiko**: Aiko, the researcher, heavily relies on attaching and annotating PDFs (US-08, US-10). By excluding these, we fail to deliver core value to this persona in the MVP. This may result in low adoption among researchers and negative feedback on the lack of multimedia support.

4.  **Monetization Delay**: Attachments are a key differentiator for the Plus tier. Delaying US-08 reduces the immediate perceived value of the upgrade path, potentially slowing down the **Paid Conversion** metric in the first 6 months.

## Core Sections (Overview through User Stories)

## 1. Overview

Inkwell is a fast, private, offline-first note-taking application designed for web, iOS, and Android platforms. The core value proposition rests on four pillars: speed, privacy, seamless synchronicity, and **lightweight collaboration**. Unlike cloud-centric competitors that require constant connectivity, Inkwell treats local data as the source of truth, syncing changes only when connectivity is available. This architecture ensures that users can capture, retrieve, and share information instantly, regardless of their network status. Early-access user demand and key prospect requirements from law firms and research groups have highlighted the need for secure sharing and annotation features, prompting the inclusion of link-based sharing and threaded comments in the initial release.

**Product Summary**
Inkwell allows users to create rich-text notes with Markdown shortcuts, organize them into hierarchical notebooks and flat tags, and sync across devices. The application supports attachments, including images and PDFs, and introduces **collaboration primitives** such as generating secure share links (View/Comment/Edit) and threaded comments with @mentions. Future support for web clipping and PDF annotation remains on the roadmap.

**Target Audience**
The primary users are knowledge workers who value privacy and speed: students capturing lectures, consultants documenting meetings, and researchers managing large volumes of unstructured data. **Collaborative workflows** are specifically targeted at teams requiring secure, auditable note sharing, such as legal teams and academic research groups.

**Business Model**
The application follows a freemium model:
- **Free Tier**: Up to 3 devices, 500 MB attachment storage, no version history, limited share links (e.g., up to 5 active links).
- **Inkwell Plus (€4/month)**: Unlimited devices, 10 GB attachment storage, 30 days of version history, unlimited share links, advanced activity history, and priority support.

**Technical Context**
The application must be offline-first. All CRUD operations happen locally against a persistent local store (SQLite/Realm/IndexedDB depending on platform). Background jobs handle bi-directional sync with the cloud backend when connectivity is restored. **Collaboration features (sharing, comments) must also function offline**, queuing changes for sync upon reconnection. Conflict resolution strategies must be defined and tested rigorously for both local edits and concurrent comments/shares.

## 2. Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals

1.  **Instant Interaction**: The UI must remain responsive (<16ms frame time) even when interacting with large datasets (10,000+ notes). Opening a single note (<1 MB) must happen in <300ms (p95) on mid-range mobile devices.
2.  **True Offline Capability**: Users must be able to create, edit, delete, search, and organize notes without any internet connection. Sync must be transparent and eventual.
3.  **Cross-Platform Consistency**: The core feature set (create, edit, organize, sync) must work identically on iOS, Android, and Web. The native feel is crucial; we are not building a wrapped web app for mobile.
4.  **Privacy by Design**: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) is not required for v1, but data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). We must demonstrate compliance with GDPR/CCPA standards.
5.  **Fast Search**: Full-text search across 10,000 notes must return results in <500ms (p95) offline.
6.  **Collaboration Adoption**: Achieve a **15% adoption rate** of collaboration features (creating a share link or posting a comment) among active users within the first 3 months of launch, validating the strategic pivot to include these features.

### Non-Goals

1.  **Real-Time Multiplayer Text Editing**: We will **not** support simultaneous, real-time text editing (CRDTs/OT) on the same note in v1. While share links with "Edit" permission are supported, changes sync asynchronously. True real-time cursor presence and live text merging are deferred to post-MVP to manage complexity.
2.  **Real-Time Co-Editing of PDFs**: **Explicitly out of scope**: We will not support multiple users simultaneously annotating or editing a PDF in real-time. PDF annotation is single-user, per-device.
3.  **Advanced Database Features**: We will not implement relational databases, formulas, or backlinks (Obsidian-style) in v1. The focus is on linear text and hierarchical organization.
4.  **Web Clipper for All Browsers**: In v1, we will support a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox only. Safari is deferred to post-MVP.
5.  **Video/Audio Recording**: Direct recording of audio/video into the editor is out of scope. Users can attach existing files, but recording logic is too complex for the first release.
6.  **Native Widget Customization**: While widgets are needed for quick capture, deep customization options (changing colors, data points displayed) are post-MVP.

## 8. Open Questions

*   **Conflict Resolution Granularity**: Should we use block-level diffs or full-note snapshots for conflict resolution? Block-level is better for UX but significantly more complex to implement and debug. Current assumption: Full-note snapshots with user choice, but this needs final engineering sign-off.
*   **Search Index Storage Budget**: What is the maximum allowable disk space for the local search index on low-storage devices (e.g., 64GB iPhone SE)? If a user exceeds this, do we degrade search performance or disable full-text search for older notes?
*   **Clock Skew Handling**: How should the sync engine handle devices with significant clock drift (>5 minutes) to ensure correct "last-write-wins" logic? We need to decide if we rely solely on device time or incorporate a logical clock (Lamport timestamp) in v1.
*   **Offline Sync Queue Overflow**: If a user makes 500+ edits while offline for several days, what is the maximum size/depth of the local sync queue before we force a partial sync or warn the user? We need to prevent app crashes from memory exhaustion.
*   **Markdown Compatibility Scope**: Do we strictly support CommonMark, or do we extend to support GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) for tables and task lists? Aiko and Daniel have requested table support, but tables are complex to edit with keyboard shortcuts on mobile.
*   **Beta Migration Path**: How do we migrate existing local-only data from the prototype to the new sync-enabled schema without requiring a full re-sync? We need to ensure users do not lose data during the upgrade.
*   **Collaboration Permission Inheritance**: When a notebook is shared as an "Editor", does a new note created within that notebook automatically inherit the share link's permission level, or does the owner need to explicitly share each new note? This impacts the "Shared Notebooks" (US-19) implementation complexity.
*   **Comment Thread Retention**: If a note is shared and comments are added, what happens to the comment history if the share link is revoked? Do the comments remain visible to the original author and other valid users, or are they hidden? This has privacy implications for legal and research users.
*   **Mention Notification Latency**: What is the acceptable latency for @mention notifications? Should we send push notifications immediately even if the mentioner is offline, or only upon sync? This affects the perceived responsiveness of collaboration.

## Update Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)

**NFR-10: Collaboration Latency**
Remote edits from a co-editor appear on other screens within 200 milliseconds (p95) on a normal network connection.

**NFR-11: Conflict-free Merge**
Concurrent and offline edits must merge without data loss, utilizing a conflict-free merge approach.

**NFR-12: Access Revocation Latency**
Revoking a share link or a person's access takes effect within 5 seconds on every device.

**NFR-13: Audit Log Retention**
Sharing and permission changes are recorded in an audit log retained for 1 year.

## Update MVP Cut

## 7. MVP Cut

To meet the release date with a 14-person team, the MVP scope prioritizes the core "capture, organize, retrieve, sync" loop while introducing the lowest-friction collaboration primitives (link sharing and threaded comments) to address immediate demand from high-value prospects like law firms and research groups. We prioritize data integrity and speed, deferring complex real-time multiplayer features to ensure stability.

### In the MVP

The following ten user stories are included in the initial release:

*   **US-01: Create a note** (Mandatory: Core functionality)
*   **US-02: Edit with Markdown shortcuts** (Mandatory: Core editing experience)
*   **US-05: Full-text search** (Mandatory: Core value for Daniel)
*   **US-06: Work offline** (Mandatory: Core architectural guarantee)
*   **US-07: Sync across devices** (Mandatory: Core value for Maya)
*   **US-03: Organise notes in notebooks** (Chosen: Critical for Daniel’s client-based organization and Maya’s course separation. Without this, the app is an unusable flat list for power users.)
*   **US-04: Tag notes** (Chosen: Complements notebooks for cross-cutting organization, essential for Aiko’s and Daniel’s cross-referencing needs.)
*   **US-12: Trash and restore** (Chosen: Essential for user trust. Accidental deletion is the highest risk to user retention for a note-taking app. Implementing a robust trash system is lower complexity than attachment syncing and prevents catastrophic data loss complaints.)
*   **US-16: Share a note by link** (Chosen: Lightweight entry point for collaboration. Addresses key prospect demand for sharing specific artifacts without building a full real-time engine. Low complexity: leverages existing sync infrastructure with simple token-based access.)
*   **US-18: Comments and mentions** (Chosen: Critical for feedback loops in law and research contexts. Allows asynchronous collaboration on specific passages. Can be implemented as a separate data structure linked to the note, avoiding the complexity of merging concurrent text edits.)

### After the MVP

The following ten stories are deferred to post-MVP releases (v1.1+):

*   **US-08: Attach images and PDFs** (Deferred due to high complexity in binary sync, storage limits enforcement, and UI rendering across platforms. Attachments are a significant source of sync conflicts and storage costs.)
*   **US-09: Clip a web page** (Deferred as it requires a browser extension and content extraction heuristics, which are distinct from the core app.)
*   **US-10: Annotate a PDF** (Deferred as it depends on US-08 and requires a complex PDF rendering/annotation engine.)
*   **US-11: Pin and favourite notes** (Deferred as a nice-to-have UX improvement; users can use a notebook named "Pinned" as a workaround.)
*   **US-13: Export notes** (Deferred as PDF generation engines are heavy and buggy; initial focus is on internal note-taking. Markdown export is simple but bundled with PDF for v1.1.)
*   **US-14: Version history** (Deferred as Plus feature; requires significant storage overhead and UI for diffs.)
*   **US-15: Lock a note** (Deferred as it adds security implementation complexity; app-level lock is sufficient for MVP.)
*   **US-17: Real-time co-editing** (Deferred: Requires a complex CRDT implementation to meet p95 latency requirements and offline merge guarantees. The engineering cost is too high for the MVP timeline, and the complexity risks destabilizing the core sync engine.)
*   **US-19: Shared notebooks** (Deferred: Requires complex permission management and notebook-level sharing logic. Distinct from note-level sharing in US-16, it introduces significant UI and backend complexity regarding recursive permission inheritance and notification management.)
*   **US-20: Activity history** (Deferred: Requires significant storage overhead for audit logs and complex UI for filtering events. Valuable for enterprise transparency but not essential for initial adoption compared to basic sharing and commenting.)

### Risks of the Cut

1.  **Real-Time Expectations vs. Asynchronous Reality**: Users familiar with Notion or Google Docs may expect live co-editing immediately. Offering only comments and link sharing might be perceived as "slow" collaboration. If multiple users edit a shared note via link, conflicts will arise without real-time cursor visibility, potentially leading to frustration and support tickets.
2.  **Offline Merge Complexity for Comments**: While real-time co-editing is deferred, US-16 and US-18 still rely on the sync engine. Ensuring that comments added via a shared link merge seamlessly with local edits made offline by the owner adds non-trivial edge-case testing. We must ensure comment threads do not disrupt the note's text sync logic.
3.  **Limited Notebook Collaboration**: By deferring US-19 (Shared Notebooks), high-value prospects like law firms cannot easily share entire case files or projects as a unit. They must share individual notes, which is tedious and prone to error (e.g., forgetting to share a new note). This may stall enterprise adoption and force them to use competitors with better project-level sharing.
4.  **Media Gap Persists for Researchers**: The original risk regarding Aiko (researcher) needing PDFs remains. Adding comments helps, but without US-08/US-10, she cannot annotate the PDFs themselves, only text notes. This still limits researcher adoption, as they may feel the tool is incomplete for their primary workflow.
5.  **Sync Engine Load**: Introducing link sharing and comments increases the read/write load on the sync engine and permission checks. While less complex than real-time co-editing, it still introduces new failure modes (e.g., revoked links failing to propagate immediately) that must be thoroughly tested to meet the 5-second revocation SLA.

Inkwell is a fast, private, offline-first note-taking application designed for web, iOS, and Android platforms. The core value proposition rests on four pillars: speed, privacy, seamless synchronicity, and **lightweight collaboration**. Unlike cloud-centric competitors that require constant connectivity, Inkwell treats local data as the source of truth, syncing changes only when connectivity is available. This architecture ensures that users can capture, retrieve, and share information instantly, regardless of their network status. Early-access user demand and key prospect requirements from law firms and research groups have highlighted the need for secure sharing and annotation features, prompting the inclusion of link-based sharing and threaded comments in the initial release.

**Product Summary**
Inkwell allows users to create rich-text notes with Markdown shortcuts, organize them into hierarchical notebooks and flat tags, and sync across devices. The application supports attachments, including images and PDFs, and introduces **collaboration primitives** such as generating secure share links (View/Comment/Edit) and threaded comments with @mentions. Future support for web clipping and PDF annotation remains on the roadmap.

**Target Audience**
The primary users are knowledge workers who value privacy and speed: students capturing lectures, consultants documenting meetings, and researchers managing large volumes of unstructured data. **Collaborative workflows** are specifically targeted at teams requiring secure, auditable note sharing, such as legal teams and academic research groups.

**Business Model**
The application follows a freemium model:
- **Free Tier**: Up to 3 devices, 500 MB attachment storage, no version history, limited share links (e.g., up to 5 active links).
- **Inkwell Plus (€4/month)**: Unlimited devices, 10 GB attachment storage, 30 days of version history, unlimited share links, advanced activity history, and priority support.

**Technical Context**
The application must be offline-first. All CRUD operations happen locally against a persistent local store (SQLite/Realm/IndexedDB depending on platform). Background jobs handle bi-directional sync with the cloud backend when connectivity is restored. **Collaboration features (sharing, comments) must also function offline**, queuing changes for sync upon reconnection. Conflict resolution strategies must be defined and tested rigorously for both local edits and concurrent comments/shares.

## 2. Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals

1.  **Instant Interaction**: The UI must remain responsive (<16ms frame time) even when interacting with large datasets (10,000+ notes). Opening a single note (<1 MB) must happen in <300ms (p95) on mid-range mobile devices.
2.  **True Offline Capability**: Users must be able to create, edit, delete, search, and organize notes without any internet connection. Sync must be transparent and eventual.
3.  **Cross-Platform Consistency**: The core feature set (create, edit, organize, sync) must work identically on iOS, Android, and Web. The native feel is crucial; we are not building a wrapped web app for mobile.
4.  **Privacy by Design**: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) is not required for v1, but data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). We must demonstrate compliance with GDPR/CCPA standards.
5.  **Fast Search**: Full-text search across 10,000 notes must return results in <500ms (p95) offline.
6.  **Collaboration Adoption**: Achieve a **15% adoption rate** of collaboration features (creating a share link or posting a comment) among active users within the first 3 months of launch, validating the strategic pivot to include these features.

### Non-Goals

1.  **Real-Time Multiplayer Text Editing**: We will **not** support simultaneous, real-time text editing (CRDTs/OT) on the same note in v1. While share links with "Edit" permission are supported, changes sync asynchronously. True real-time cursor presence and live text merging are deferred to post-MVP to manage complexity.
2.  **Real-Time Co-Editing of PDFs**: **Explicitly out of scope**: We will not support multiple users simultaneously annotating or editing a PDF in real-time. PDF annotation is single-user, per-device.
3.  **Advanced Database Features**: We will not implement relational databases, formulas, or backlinks (Obsidian-style) in v1. The focus is on linear text and hierarchical organization.
4.  **Web Clipper for All Browsers**: In v1, we will support a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox only. Safari is deferred to post-MVP.
5.  **Video/Audio Recording**: Direct recording of audio/video into the editor is out of scope. Users can attach existing files, but recording logic is too complex for the first release.
6.  **Native Widget Customization**: While widgets are needed for quick capture, deep customization options (changing colors, data points displayed) are post-MVP.

## 8. Open Questions

*   **Conflict Resolution Granularity**: Should we use block-level diffs or full-note snapshots for conflict resolution? Block-level is better for UX but significantly more complex to implement and debug. Current assumption: Full-note snapshots with user choice, but this needs final engineering sign-off.
*   **Search Index Storage Budget**: What is the maximum allowable disk space for the local search index on low-storage devices (e.g., 64GB iPhone SE)? If a user exceeds this, do we degrade search performance or disable full-text search for older notes?
*   **Clock Skew Handling**: How should the sync engine handle devices with significant clock drift (>5 minutes) to ensure correct "last-write-wins" logic? We need to decide if we rely solely on device time or incorporate a logical clock (Lamport timestamp) in v1.
*   **Offline Sync Queue Overflow**: If a user makes 500+ edits while offline for several days, what is the maximum size/depth of the local sync queue before we force a partial sync or warn the user? We need to prevent app crashes from memory exhaustion.
*   **Markdown Compatibility Scope**: Do we strictly support CommonMark, or do we extend to support GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) for tables and task lists? Aiko and Daniel have requested table support, but tables are complex to edit with keyboard shortcuts on mobile.
*   **Beta Migration Path**: How do we migrate existing local-only data from the prototype to the new sync-enabled schema without requiring a full re-sync? We need to ensure users do not lose data during the upgrade.
*   **Collaboration Permission Inheritance**: When a notebook is shared as an "Editor", does a new note created within that notebook automatically inherit the share link's permission level, or does the owner need to explicitly share each new note? This impacts the "Shared Notebooks" (US-19) implementation complexity.
*   **Comment Thread Retention**: If a note is shared and comments are added, what happens to the comment history if the share link is revoked? Do the comments remain visible to the original author and other valid users, or are they hidden? This has privacy implications for legal and research users.
*   **Mention Notification Latency**: What is the acceptable latency for @mention notifications? Should we send push notifications immediately even if the mentioner is offline, or only upon sync? This affects the perceived responsiveness of collaboration.

parts.title: Update Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)
parts.body:
**NFR-10: Collaboration Latency**
Remote edits from a co-editor appear on other screens within 200 milliseconds (p95) on a normal network connection.

**NFR-11: Conflict-free Merge**
Concurrent and offline edits must merge without data loss, utilizing a conflict-free merge approach.

**NFR-12: Access Revocation Latency**
Revoking a share link or a person's access takes effect within 5 seconds on every device.

**NFR-13: Audit Log Retention**
Sharing and permission changes are recorded in an audit log retained for 1 year.

parts.title: Update MVP Cut
parts.body:
## 7. MVP Cut

To meet the release date with a 14-person team, the MVP scope prioritizes the core "capture, organize, retrieve, sync" loop while introducing the lowest-friction collaboration primitives (link sharing and threaded comments) to address immediate demand from high-value prospects like law firms and research groups. We prioritize data integrity and speed, deferring complex real-time multiplayer features to ensure stability.

### In the MVP

The following ten user stories are included in the initial release:

*   **US-01: Create a note** (Mandatory: Core functionality)
*   **US-02: Edit with Markdown shortcuts** (Mandatory: Core editing experience)
*   **US-05: Full-text search** (Mandatory: Core value for Daniel)
*   **US-06: Work offline** (Mandatory: Core architectural guarantee)
*   **US-07: Sync across devices** (Mandatory: Core value for Maya)
*   **US-03: Organise notes in notebooks** (Chosen: Critical for Daniel’s client-based organization and Maya’s course separation. Without this, the app is an unusable flat list for power users.)
*   **US-04: Tag notes** (Chosen: Complements notebooks for cross-cutting organization, essential for Aiko’s and Daniel’s cross-referencing needs.)
*   **US-12: Trash and restore** (Chosen: Essential for user trust. Accidental deletion is the highest risk to user retention for a note-taking app. Implementing a robust trash system is lower complexity than attachment syncing and prevents catastrophic data loss complaints.)
*   **US-16: Share a note by link** (Chosen: Lightweight entry point for collaboration. Addresses key prospect demand for sharing specific artifacts without building a full real-time engine. Low complexity: leverages existing sync infrastructure with simple token-based access.)
*   **US-18: Comments and mentions** (Chosen: Critical for feedback loops in law and research contexts. Allows asynchronous collaboration on specific passages. Can be implemented as a separate data structure linked to the note, avoiding the complexity of merging concurrent text edits.)

### After the MVP

The following ten stories are deferred to post-MVP releases (v1.1+):

*   **US-08: Attach images and PDFs** (Deferred due to high complexity in binary sync, storage limits enforcement, and UI rendering across platforms. Attachments are a significant source of sync conflicts and storage costs.)
*   **US-09: Clip a web page** (Deferred as it requires a browser extension and content extraction heuristics, which are distinct from the core app.)
*   **US-10: Annotate a PDF** (Deferred as it depends on US-08 and requires a complex PDF rendering/annotation engine.)
*   **US-11: Pin and favourite notes** (Deferred as a nice-to-have UX improvement; users can use a notebook named "Pinned" as a workaround.)
*   **US-13: Export notes** (Deferred as PDF generation engines are heavy and buggy; initial focus is on internal note-taking. Markdown export is simple but bundled with PDF for v1.1.)
*   **US-14: Version history** (Deferred as Plus feature; requires significant storage overhead and UI for diffs.)
*   **US-15: Lock a note** (Deferred as it adds security implementation complexity; app-level lock is sufficient for MVP.)
*   **US-17: Real-time co-editing** (Deferred: Requires a complex CRDT implementation to meet p95 latency requirements and offline merge guarantees. The engineering cost is too high for the MVP timeline, and the complexity risks destabilizing the core sync engine.)
*   **US-19: Shared notebooks** (Deferred: Requires complex permission management and notebook-level sharing logic. Distinct from note-level sharing in US-16, it introduces significant UI and backend complexity regarding recursive permission inheritance and notification management.)
*   **US-20: Activity history** (Deferred: Requires significant storage overhead for audit logs and complex UI for filtering events. Valuable for enterprise transparency but not essential for initial adoption compared to basic sharing and commenting.)

### Risks of the Cut

1.  **Real-Time Expectations vs. Asynchronous Reality**: Users familiar with Notion or Google Docs may expect live co-editing immediately. Offering only comments and link sharing might be perceived as "slow" collaboration. If multiple users edit a shared note via link, conflicts will arise without real-time cursor visibility, potentially leading to frustration and support tickets.
2.  **Offline Merge Complexity for Comments**: While real-time co-editing is deferred, US-16 and US-18 still rely on the sync engine. Ensuring that comments added via a shared link merge seamlessly with local edits made offline by the owner adds non-trivial edge-case testing. We must ensure comment threads do not disrupt the note's text sync logic.
3.  **Limited Notebook Collaboration**: By deferring US-19 (Shared Notebooks), high-value prospects like law firms cannot easily share entire case files or projects as a unit. They must share individual notes, which is tedious and prone to error (e.g., forgetting to share a new note). This may stall enterprise adoption and force them to use competitors with better project-level sharing.
4.  **Media Gap Persists for Researchers**: The original risk regarding Aiko (researcher) needing PDFs remains. Adding comments helps, but without US-08/US-10, she cannot annotate the PDFs themselves, only text notes. This still limits researcher adoption, as they may feel the tool is incomplete for their primary workflow.
5.  **Sync Engine Load**: Introducing link sharing and comments increases the read/write load on the sync engine and permission checks. While less complex than real-time co-editing, it still introduces new failure modes (e.g., revoked links failing to propagate immediately) that must be thoroughly tested to meet the 5-second revocation SLA.

## 6. Success Metrics

The following metrics will be tracked to evaluate the success of the launch and the health of the product over the first six months.

| Metric | Definition | Target at 6 months after launch |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Activation Rate** | Percentage of new signups who create at least one note within 24 hours of registration. | 40% |
| **D30 Retention** | Percentage of users from a given signup cohort who open the app on Day 30 post-signup. | 15% |
| **Sync Success Rate** | Percentage of sync operations that complete without error within the 10-second target window. | 95% |
| **Search Latency (P95)** | The 95th percentile of time taken to return search results for a query in an offline index of 10,000+ notes. | < 500 ms |
| **Paid Conversion** | Percentage of active free users who upgrade to the Inkwell Plus plan. | 2.0% |
| **Collaboration Adoption** | Percentage of active notebooks that have at least one shared link or threaded comment interaction in the past 30 days. | 15% |
